section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on most urban streets in Mississippi when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:40 mph
note: Mississippi sets the default speed limit in urban areas at 30 mph when no other limit is posted. Many new drivers assume 25 mph (common in other states), but Mississippi's default urban limit is 30 mph. Always check posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on most Mississippi interstate highways for passenger vehicles?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: Mississippi's standard interstate speed limit is 70 mph for passenger vehicles on most rural interstate sections. Urban sections through Jackson or other cities may have lower posted limits. Always follow the posted sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in Mississippi school zones when children are present?
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: Mississippi school zones have a 20 mph speed limit when children are present or warning lights are active. This is lower than many states' 25 mph limit. Slow down well in advance of school zones and remain alert for children near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Mississippi's GDL program, at what age can a teenager apply for a learner's permit?
options: a:14,b:15,c:16,d:15 and a half
note: In Mississippi, teens can apply for a learner's permit at age 15. After meeting supervised driving requirements, they become eligible for an intermediate license at age 16 after 1 year of supervised practice including at least 15 hours at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Mississippi's GDL program requires permit holders to complete at least how many supervised nighttime driving hours?
options: a:5 hours,b:10 hours,c:15 hours,d:20 hours
note: Mississippi requires GDL permit holders to complete at least 50 hours of supervised driving practice, of which at least 15 hours must be at night. Mississippi's 15-hour nighttime requirement is higher than many other states and reflects the importance of building nighttime driving skills before driving alone after dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Mississippi's GDL nighttime restrictions, teens under 17 with an intermediate license may not drive during which hours?
options: a:10 PM to 5 AM,b:11 PM to 5 AM,c:Midnight to 5 AM,d:Midnight to 6 AM
note: Mississippi restricts drivers under 17 with an intermediate license from driving between midnight and 5 AM unless accompanied by a licensed adult age 21 or older. Exceptions apply for work, school activities, and emergencies. The curfew is midnight — not 10 PM or 11 PM.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in Mississippi is:
note: Mississippi, like all U.S. states, sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. A BAC at or above this level establishes impairment under Mississippi law regardless of how the driver looks or acts. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Mississippi's zero tolerance law, what BAC level is illegal for a driver under 21?
options: a:Any measurable amount — 0.00%,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.08%
note: Mississippi's zero tolerance law for underage drivers sets the illegal BAC threshold at 0.02%. A driver under 21 with a BAC of 0.02% or higher faces DUI charges and license suspension. This is considerably lower than the adult standard of 0.08%.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Mississippi's implied consent law, a driver who refuses a chemical test after a DUI stop will:
options: a:Face no legal penalty,b:Have their license suspended automatically for 90 days,c:Only receive a written warning,d:Lose their license permanently
note: Mississippi's implied consent law means that driving on state roads constitutes consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal triggers a 90-day license suspension. The refusal can also be presented as evidence of consciousness of guilt at trial. Refusing rarely benefits the driver legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Mississippi's seatbelt law requires which vehicle occupants to be buckled?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Driver and front-seat passengers only,c:All occupants in all seating positions,d:Only occupants under age 21
note: Mississippi requires all vehicle occupants — front and rear seats — to wear a seatbelt. Mississippi has primary enforcement, meaning an officer can stop a vehicle solely because a front-seat occupant is unbuckled, without any other violation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a Mississippi highway, the Move Over law requires you to:
options: a:Stop completely until the vehicle drives away,b:Move over only for police or fire vehicles,c:Move one lane away if safe, or reduce to a safe speed if a lane change isn't possible,d:Only slow down when instructed by an officer
note: Mississippi's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, towing, or utility vehicle with flashing lights. If a safe lane change is not possible, slow to a safe speed for conditions. Violating this law carries significant fines.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane Mississippi road, a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights. What must drivers traveling in BOTH directions do?
options: a:Only drivers behind the bus must stop,b:Slow to 20 mph and pass carefully,c:Stop at least 20 feet from the bus in both directions until red lights stop flashing,d:Stop only if children are visible outside the bus
note: On an undivided two-lane road in Mississippi, vehicles in both directions must stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights. Wait until the arm retracts and the lights stop before proceeding. On a divided highway with a raised median, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the recommended following distance in Mississippi under normal driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Mississippi recommends a 3-second following distance under normal conditions. Pick a fixed landmark and count 3 seconds from when the car ahead passes it. In rain, fog, or on slick roads, double it to at least 6 seconds. More space means more reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same moment as a driver directly to your right. Who goes first?
options: a:You go first because you plan to go straight,b:The driver to your right has the right of way,c:Whoever has their turn signal on goes first,d:Both must wait for an officer to direct traffic
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to your RIGHT has the right of way. Yield to the vehicle on your right and wait for it to proceed before you move. This is the universal tie-breaker rule at stop signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a Mississippi two-lane road, a solid yellow line is painted on YOUR side of the center. This means:
options: a:You may pass if the road looks clear for 500 feet,b:Passing is prohibited — do not cross the center line to overtake,c:You are entering a designated passing zone,d:The road is about to narrow
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means you are prohibited from crossing the center line to pass. These markings appear where visibility is limited — hills, curves, and near intersections. A dashed yellow line on your side indicates that passing is permitted when the road ahead is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning right on a red light in Mississippi is:
options: a:Prohibited statewide,b:Permitted after a full stop and yielding, unless a sign says otherwise,c:Permitted without stopping if no vehicles are approaching,d:Allowed only between 6 AM and 10 PM
note: Mississippi permits right turns on red after a complete stop and yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic, unless a 'No Turn on Red' sign is posted. Always come to a full stop and verify the intersection is clear before proceeding. Some intersections — particularly urban ones — prohibit the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean in Mississippi?
options: a:Caution — slow and proceed,b:Yield to cross traffic, then proceed when clear,c:Stop completely, yield to all traffic, then proceed when safe,d:The signal is out of order — treat as uncontrolled
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to all vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed when the way is clearly safe. A flashing yellow light means caution — slow down but a full stop is not required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must headlights be used on Mississippi roads?
options: a:Only between 1 AM and 5 AM,b:Only when it is actively raining,c:From sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is less than 500 feet,d:Only on rural roads and state highways
note: Mississippi requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is reduced to less than 500 feet due to weather or road conditions. Many drivers forget to turn on headlights in light drizzle or at dusk — both situations when lights are legally required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are making a left turn at a green light. Oncoming traffic is still moving through the intersection. You should:
options: a:Proceed immediately — the green light gives you right of way,b:Enter the intersection and wait for a safe gap before completing the turn,c:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then complete the turn when safe,d:Only turn when a dedicated left-turn arrow appears
note: Even on a solid green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic before completing a left turn. Enter the intersection to position yourself, wait for a clear gap, then complete the turn. Left-turn crashes are among the most common — patience is critical.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most Mississippi rural two-lane highways when no sign is posted?
options: a:45 mph,b:50 mph,c:55 mph,d:60 mph
note: The default rural highway speed limit in Mississippi is 55 mph when no other limit is posted. On interstate highways, the limit is higher — typically 70 mph. Always verify with posted signs, especially in areas with frequent driveways or intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Mississippi highway and see a stationary tow truck on the shoulder with flashing lights. Under the Move Over law, you must:
options: a:Only yield if the tow truck is blocking your lane,b:Move one lane away or slow to a safe speed if a lane change is not possible,c:Stop and wait for the tow truck to finish,d:Activate your hazard lights and maintain speed
note: Mississippi's Move Over law explicitly includes tow trucks and recovery vehicles — not just police or fire trucks. Move one lane away if it is safe to do so. If the road does not allow a safe lane change, reduce speed significantly. Tow truck operators are frequently injured by passing vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yellow diamond-shaped road sign with an arrow curving sharply to the right indicate?
options: a:You must turn right at the next intersection,b:A sharp curve or turn to the right is ahead — reduce speed,c:A one-way street ahead — prepare to yield,d:An exit ramp is approaching on the right
note: A yellow diamond sign with a sharp curve arrow warns of an upcoming sharp turn. Reduce your speed before the curve — entering a curve too fast is a leading cause of run-off-road crashes. Always reduce speed before curves, not during them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which Mississippi law prohibits texting while driving?
options: a:Mississippi has no texting-while-driving ban,b:Texting is prohibited only for drivers under 18,c:Mississippi prohibits texting while driving for all drivers,d:Texting is prohibited only in school zones and construction zones
note: Mississippi prohibits all drivers from texting while driving. Reading, composing, or sending a text while the vehicle is in motion is illegal statewide. Distracted driving — especially texting — is one of the leading causes of crashes and fatalities in Mississippi.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you change lanes or reduce speed to safely pass a stopped emergency vehicle in Mississippi?
options: a:Only when the emergency vehicle's lights are flashing and an officer is visible,b:Whenever a vehicle on the roadside has hazard lights on,c:Any time an authorized emergency, law enforcement, towing, or utility vehicle is stopped with flashing lights,d:Only when the stopped vehicle is partially in the travel lane
note: Mississippi's Move Over law requires a lane change or speed reduction whenever any authorized emergency, law enforcement, towing, or utility vehicle is stopped on or near the roadway with flashing lights — regardless of whether the vehicle is fully on the shoulder or whether an officer is visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What shape and color is used for regulatory signs such as speed limit signs in Mississippi?
options: a:Yellow diamond,b:Red octagon,c:White rectangle,d:Blue circle
note: Regulatory signs — including speed limit signs, turn prohibitions, and one-way signs — are white rectangles with black text and borders. Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. Red octagon (stop sign), yellow diamond (warning), and green rectangle (guide) all serve different purposes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An uncontrolled intersection in Mississippi means an intersection with no signs or signals. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The vehicle traveling on the larger road,b:The vehicle that is going straight, not turning,c:The driver on the LEFT yields to the driver on the RIGHT,d:Whoever arrives first always proceeds
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This is the fundamental right-of-way rule for intersections without signs or signals in Mississippi and across the United States.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in fog on a Mississippi highway. Which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beams for maximum illumination,b:Low beams or fog lights if equipped,c:Only your parking lights,d:No headlights — they reflect off the fog
note: In fog, use low beams or dedicated fog lights. High beams reflect off fog droplets and create glare that reduces your visibility and blinds oncoming drivers. Low beams aim downward, reducing reflection. Pull over and wait if fog is too dense to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before a Mississippi teen can get an intermediate license at age 16, they must hold their learner's permit for at least:
options: a:90 days,b:6 months,c:1 full year,d:2 years
note: Mississippi requires permit holders to hold the learner's permit for at least 1 full year before upgrading to an intermediate license at age 16. They must also complete 50 hours of supervised practice (15 at night). Both the time and driving-hours requirements must be met.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach a crosswalk in Mississippi and a pedestrian is standing on the curb with a white cane. This indicates:
options: a:They are waiting for a bus,b:They are a visually impaired pedestrian and you must stop and yield,c:They are a crossing guard — wait for their signal,d:No special action is required unless they step into the street
note: A white cane indicates a visually impaired or blind pedestrian. Mississippi law gives these pedestrians absolute right of way at all crossings, and drivers must stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has completely cleared the roadway. White-cane pedestrian right of way is a federal and state requirement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching with lights and siren from any direction in Mississippi?
options: a:Maintain your speed to avoid disrupting traffic flow,b:Stop immediately wherever you are,c:Pull to the right edge of the road and stop,d:Move to the center lane to create space
note: Mississippi law requires drivers to immediately pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from any direction. Remain stopped until the vehicle has completely passed. Never block an intersection — pull through it first if necessary, then stop on the right.

question: If a steady green light turns yellow and you are already in the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the intersection.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Clear the intersection safely and promptly.,d:Back up slowly.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely and without unnecessary delay. Do not stop suddenly in the middle of the intersection or back up, as that can confuse other drivers and increase the risk of a collision.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and continue driving.,c:Drink coffee and keep driving.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time — stop in a safe place to rest or switch drivers if possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing in any marked no passing zone.,b:Passing over a railroad crossing.,c:Both passing in no passing zones and over railroad crossings are illegal.
note: Passing is illegal where signs or pavement markings prohibit it, such as in marked no‑passing zones, and it is also unlawful to pass at or on a railroad crossing. Both of these situations are designed to protect drivers where visibility or conditions make passing especially dangerous.

question: What problems can a worn suspension cause?
options: a:Vehicle control problems, making the car harder to steer and less stable.,b:Squealing brakes only.,c:Excess slack in the steering column only.
note: A worn or damaged suspension can make the vehicle harder to control, especially when turning, braking, or driving over bumps. It reduces stability and can increase stopping distance or cause uneven tire wear. Because suspension affects how your tires stay in contact with the road, it is critical for safe steering and handling.

question: If a lane has an overhead sign showing an arrow with the word ONLY, what must you do?
options: a:Travel only in the direction shown by the arrow.,b:Always change lanes when you see this sign.,c:Look for a destination sign to decide where to go.
note: An overhead lane control sign with an arrow and the word ONLY means that from that lane you are permitted to make only the movement shown by the arrow, such as left turn only or straight only. You must follow the direction indicated and should choose your lane in advance based on where you need to go.

question: Slowing down just to look at crashes or unusual events:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.
note: Slowing down just to look at crashes or unusual events is called rubbernecking. It disrupts normal traffic flow, creates sudden slowdowns, and can trigger rear-end collisions and traffic jams. You should keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a safe, steady speed instead of slowing to look.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.
note: U‑turns are especially dangerous where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on or near curves or hills. Because your view and others’ view of you are blocked, a vehicle may approach quickly and hit you. Only make U‑turns where they are legal, clearly visible for a long distance, and safe.

question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Time
note: Once alcohol is in your bloodstream, only time allows your body to break it down and lower your BAC. Coffee, food, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how fast your liver processes alcohol. You must allow enough time to pass before driving.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what is the proper procedure?
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if it is safe to do so.,b:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first passing car.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull as far onto the shoulder as possible, turn on your hazard flashers, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt on if it is safe. Standing or walking near high‑speed traffic is very dangerous, so you should only exit the vehicle if there is an immediate safety concern.

question: Where should drivers be especially alert to children?
options: a:School zones and playgrounds, residential neighborhoods, and other areas where children gather.,b:Only at marked school crossings.,c:Only residential neighborhoods.,d:Only playgrounds.
note: Children can be unpredictable and may suddenly enter the roadway, so drivers must be especially alert anywhere children are likely to be present. This includes school zones, school bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and residential neighborhoods. Slow down, scan carefully, and be prepared to stop whenever you see children nearby.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow is displayed with a red traffic light, when may you proceed in the arrow’s direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, you may proceed.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:You must wait until the main light turns green.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in that direction. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: When should you avoid using your horn?
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:Near blind pedestrians.,c:If you might hit another vehicle.,d:To warn a car about to hit you.
note: You should not use your horn near blind pedestrians because they rely heavily on sound cues to navigate. A sudden horn blast can disorient or startle them and create a dangerous situation. Use your horn only to help prevent a collision, not to startle or punish others.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians whenever necessary to avoid hitting them, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally or not following signals. You have a legal and safety duty to avoid a collision with a pedestrian in the roadway, regardless of who has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Treat it as a stop sign and come to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Proceed since you have the right-of-way.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate?
options: a:70 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: On rural interstate highways in Mississippi, the typical maximum speed limit is 70 mph unless signs show a different limit. Always follow the posted speed limit, as it may be lower in construction zones, urban areas, or where conditions require reduced speed.

question: When exiting a freeway on a downhill ramp that curves, how should you handle your speed?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve.,b:Wait until you've entered the curve to begin braking.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: On a downhill, curving exit ramp, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve, especially going downhill, can cause skidding or loss of control. Enter the ramp at a speed that lets you steer smoothly through the curve.

question: When during rainy weather should you be most cautious when turning or stopping?
options: a:After it has been raining all day.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: The first part of a rainstorm is often the most slippery because water mixes with oil, grease, and other residues on the road surface. During roughly the first half hour of rain, you should be especially cautious when turning or stopping, as traction is reduced.

question: What important step should you take before making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions and adjust speed.,b:Increase your speed to make the turn quicker.,c:Move toward the left lane regardless of direction.
note: Before making any turn, you must check traffic in all directions and adjust your speed as needed. Look ahead, behind, and to both sides, and signal early so others know your intentions. Slow down enough to make a smooth, controlled turn.

question: If weather or light conditions require lights, which should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Interior dome light.
note: When weather or light conditions require you to use lights, you should use your low beam headlights. Low beams improve your visibility without creating glare for other drivers and are safer than high beams in fog, rain, or snow, where high beams can reflect back and reduce what you can see.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following:
options: a:Motorcycle,b:Station wagon,c:Passenger vehicle
note: When following a motorcycle, always leave extra space because motorcycles are smaller, harder to see, and can stop or change speed more quickly than larger vehicles. A greater following distance gives you more time to react if the rider brakes suddenly or swerves to avoid a hazard.

question: How should drivers approach a curve in the road?
options: a:Decrease their speed before entering the curve.,b:Increase speed to maintain momentum.,c:Maintain their normal speed.
note: Slow down before entering a curve to maintain control; accelerate again only after passing the curve's midpoint if safe.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing prohibited.,c:Passing allowed from both directions.,d:Passing allowed only during daytime.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: Are you required to obey directions given by a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:At all times when they are directing traffic.,c:Only if you see children present.
note: Drivers must always obey crossing guards near schools; their directions help protect children crossing the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If someone is merging into your lane on the freeway, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Maintain your position and speed at all costs.,b:Make room for the merging vehicle if it is safe to do so.,c:Speed up to prevent them from merging.,d:Brake sharply to let them in.
note: When traffic allows, make room to allow vehicles to merge safely into your lane.

question: At a flashing yellow traffic signal, what should you do as you approach?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before moving.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow, look, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: What can happen if you take prescription medication while drinking alcohol?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive safely.,b:It will likely make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect on driving ability.
note: Alcohol can interact with many prescription and over‑the‑counter medications to greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment. Even if the medication is legal and prescribed, combining it with alcohol can make you unsafe to drive.

question: If a large truck or bus is turning right where you also intend to turn, what should you do?
options: a:Try to cut in front of it before it completes its turn.,b:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn.,c:Squeeze between the vehicle and the curb.
note: Large trucks and buses need extra room to turn and may swing wide or use more than one lane. If you try to pass or squeeze beside them, you can be trapped or hit. Stay back and wait until the truck or bus has fully completed its turn before you turn.

question: What danger does driver fatigue most increase?
options: a:Missing an exit.,b:Being late for appointments.,c:Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue slows your reactions, reduces awareness, and can cause you to briefly nod off or fully fall asleep. When you fall asleep at the wheel, you can drift out of your lane or off the road and crash at full speed, which is extremely dangerous.

question: What color and background do temporary construction signs have?
options: a:Red background with green writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary work‑zone and construction signs in the U.S. are orange with black letters or symbols. The orange color alerts drivers to changing road conditions, workers, and equipment so they can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: Why should motorists leave extra space for children riding bicycles?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults,b:Both that they lack adult reflexes and are harder to see,c:Children always follow traffic rules,d:They do not have the same reflexes as adults
note: Children on bicycles are smaller and harder to see, and they often lack the judgment and quick reflexes of adults. They may make sudden or unpredictable moves. Leave extra space, slow down, and be especially careful near schools, neighborhoods, and parks.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Stop before crossing.,b:Slow down and cross carefully when safe.,c:Wait for the green light.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and proceed only when it is safe. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic that may be entering the intersection.

question: Which describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road and think about what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do next. They leave space, control their speed, and are ready to brake or steer safely if someone else makes a mistake.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding.,b:Stop and remain stopped; do not move in the arrow's direction.,c:Slow and proceed with caution.,d:Turn only after signaling.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped if you intend to move in the direction of the arrow. You may not turn or go in that direction until the arrow turns green or you are otherwise directed by a traffic control device or officer.

question: What does excessive speed most often lead to?
options: a:High-risk decision-making and an increased chance of crashes.,b:An improved ability to react to hazards.,c:Saving a significant amount of travel time.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards and makes crashes more likely and more severe. At higher speeds, you need more distance to stop, and even small mistakes can lead to serious collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection,b:You may continue through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear,c:Stop and yield to vehicles on the left,d:Only turn right on green
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe and allowed, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection. Green never means to speed up; always proceed at a safe, controlled speed.

question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.,d:Increase your speed slightly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to prevent this is to slow down in wet conditions and avoid sudden movements. Never use cruise control in heavy rain because you need full control of your speed.

question: How should you steer and brake when driving in inclement weather?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly,b:Steer off the road immediately,c:Drive only in low gear,d:Brake and turn abruptly to correct slides
note: In rain, snow, or other bad weather, you should steer and brake smoothly and gently. Sudden braking or sharp steering can cause your tires to lose traction and lead to a skid. Smooth inputs help your tires maintain grip on slippery roads.

question: As you near the crest of a hill, how should you drive?
options: a:Speed up slightly to crests quickly.,b:Be prepared to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed at all times.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, you cannot see what is ahead, so you must be ready to slow or stop. Reduce speed if needed and be prepared to stop for stalled vehicles, stopped traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards just over the crest.

question: If poor weather reduces your visibility, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: When weather reduces visibility, you need more space and time to react. Increasing your following distance gives you a larger safety cushion if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Avoid speeding up or driving close to oncoming traffic in poor visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline or lane closest to the centerline.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: For a left turn from a two-way street, position your vehicle in the lane nearest the centerline or in the leftmost lane available for your direction of travel. Start the turn from that lane and enter the first legal lane on the road you are turning onto.

question: In a work zone, how should you drive?
options: a:Increase your speed to get through quickly.,b:Reduce speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Maintain your usual speed throughout the zone.
note: In work zones you must slow down, follow posted work-zone speed limits, and be ready to stop suddenly for workers, equipment, or lane shifts. Driving more slowly gives you more time to react and helps protect road workers and other drivers.

question: When backing up, what is the recommended way to view behind you?
options: a:Look through the rear window while moving slowly.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Press hard on the gas to get out quickly.,d:Rely only on a backup camera.
note: When backing, turn and look directly through the rear window while moving very slowly. Use mirrors and any backup camera only as supplements. Physically looking back gives you the widest, most accurate view of people, vehicles, and obstacles behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but don't see a gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Slow down or stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a safe gap.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Maintain speed and force a gap.
note: On most freeways you should use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge smoothly. If there is no gap, you may need to slow or stop at the end of the ramp and wait until it is safe, then accelerate quickly to match traffic as you merge. Never force your way into traffic.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:To spot potential hazards earlier.,b:Because the speed limit is always higher.,c:To be able to change lanes more often.
note: On a freeway you are traveling at higher speeds, so situations develop more quickly. Looking farther ahead lets you see slowdowns, crashes, lane closures, and merging traffic early, giving you time to change lanes or adjust speed smoothly instead of braking hard at the last second.

question: If you expect to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself against the seatback.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: If you expect to be hit from behind, keep your seat belt fastened. Press your head firmly against the head restraint and brace your body against the seatback. This helps keep your body and head moving together and reduces the risk of whiplash and other injuries.

question: Where are high-beam headlights appropriate?
options: a:When within 500 feet of another vehicle.,b:On open country roads with no nearby traffic.,c:In heavy city traffic.,d:In foggy conditions.
note: High-beam headlights are for use on open roads at night when there is no oncoming traffic and no vehicle directly ahead of you. They help you see farther, but you must dim them within about 500 feet of oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle closely so you do not blind other drivers.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,c:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: When you face both an oncoming vehicle and a pedestrian ahead, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Once the lane is clear and it is safe, move over as needed and pass the pedestrian with plenty of space.

question: If your vehicle's wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed, check traffic, and when safe gradually steer back onto the road.,b:Turn sharply back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop and wait on the shoulder.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and avoid jerking the wheel. Ease off the accelerator, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, and slow down. When traffic allows and your speed is under control, gently steer back onto the pavement at a shallow angle so you don’t lose control.

question: If oncoming headlights are dazzling you at night, how should you respond?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the road and avoid looking directly at the lights.,b:Switch your headlights to high beams.,c:Turn your headlights off and on repeatedly.
note: Bright oncoming headlights can cause glare and temporary blindness. To reduce this, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide instead of looking directly at the lights. Keep your headlights on low beam and maintain a safe speed until the vehicle passes.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Follow closer than you would a passenger car.,b:Allow more distance than you would for a passenger vehicle.,c:Drive to the truck's right and wait to pass.
note: Large trucks need more time and distance to stop and have big blind spots directly behind them. When following a truck, increase your following distance so you can see the truck’s mirrors and have enough space to react if it slows or stops suddenly.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Only electronic devices that you use while driving.,c:Only passengers who shout or cause evasive action.
note: Anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving is a distraction. This includes phones, eating, adjusting controls, or interacting with passengers. Because distractions are not limited to electronics or loud passengers, the best answer is that any activity that diverts your attention from driving is a distraction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you into the lane because you have the right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into the gap when it is safe.,c:Wait until the lane clears entirely before merging.
note: When entering an interstate, you must use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and then merge into a safe gap. You do not have the right-of-way over freeway traffic and should not expect others to move for you, nor must you wait for the lane to be completely empty.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Hazard flashers only.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights so the light aims down at the road. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can create glare, making it harder to see. Parking lights or hazard flashers alone do not provide enough forward visibility for safe driving.

question: If you see pedestrians close to the roadway where you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly,c:Slow down and pass with caution
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass with extra caution. Drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and should anticipate that someone might step into the road unexpectedly, especially in residential or busy areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park facing downhill on a two-way road with no curb, how should you point your front wheels?
options: a:Left, toward the center of the road,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Straight ahead
note: On a downhill slope with no curb, turn the front wheels toward the side of the road (to the right). If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into traffic. Always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in the proper gear or park position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.
note: When changing lanes, you must always check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, and signal before moving. Abrupt or spontaneous lane changes are dangerous because other drivers do not have time to react, increasing the risk of a collision.

question: Which roadway feature tends to freeze before surrounding pavement?
options: a:A tunnel.,b:An intersection.,c:A bridge or overpass.
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze first because cold air circulates both above and below the surface, causing them to lose heat faster than regular roadways. In freezing conditions, approach bridges and overpasses more slowly and be prepared for icy patches even if the main road looks clear.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving, after positioning your seat.,b:Before you get into the car, while outside it.,c:Only when you need to use them while driving.
note: Adjust your seat first, then set your rearview and side mirrors before you start driving. This ensures you have the best possible view around your vehicle from the moment you move, reducing blind spots and the need for adjustment while in motion.

question: Approaching an intersection where the traffic signal is steady yellow and you have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you should slow down and come to a controlled stop before the crosswalk or stop line, rather than speeding up to get through.

question: If a tire blows out, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Ease off the accelerator and let the car slow down. Use the brakes gently only after you have the vehicle under control, then steer to a safe place off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from you.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: At a four‑way stop, drivers proceed in the order they arrive. You must yield to any vehicle that reached the intersection before you. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right‑of‑way. Never assume right‑of‑way; be prepared to yield to avoid a collision.

question: As your travel speed increases, what should you do to remain safe?
options: a:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Change lanes more often.,d:Reduce following distance.
note: As speed increases, you cover more distance in less time, so you need to look farther ahead to spot hazards early. Scanning well ahead gives you more time to react, change lanes, or slow down smoothly. You should also maintain a safe following distance; never reduce it at higher speeds.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b:You see a train approaching or warning devices (lights, gates, or bells) indicate a train is coming.,c:You are required to stop by law, such as when driving a school bus or certain hazardous materials vehicles.
note: You must never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks. If traffic is stopped ahead and you might be forced to stop on the tracks, wait before the crossing until you can drive all the way across safely. Stopping on the tracks is extremely dangerous because trains cannot stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a left-turn lane for an upcoming left turn and there is oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Keep your front wheels straight while waiting to turn left.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Stay centered in the designated left‑turn lane, not to the extreme left or right.
note: When preparing for a left turn, you should signal well before reaching the intersection so other drivers know your intentions. As you wait in the left‑turn lane with oncoming traffic present, keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic. Stay centered in the lane and only turn the wheels as you actually begin the turn.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road and stop if visibility is too poor,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights,c:Use your high beam headlights,d:Flash your headlights to warn others
note: In fog, slow down and use low‑beam headlights so the light does not reflect back and reduce your visibility. Increase your following distance and be prepared for sudden stops. If visibility becomes so poor that you cannot see well enough to drive safely, pull completely off the road, turn on your hazard lights, and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Force pedestrians to yield to your vehicle.,d:Honk to move pedestrians faster.
note: A green light means you may go only if the intersection is clear. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk always have the right‑of‑way, even when you have a green light or are turning. You must wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding.

question: How can you stay aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window while driving.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: To stay aware of traffic behind you, glance in your mirrors regularly—about every few seconds. This helps you notice vehicles that are following too closely, approaching quickly, or preparing to pass, so you can adjust your driving safely.

question: You must give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
options: a:In a marked crosswalk.,b:In any crosswalk, marked or unmarked, at an intersection.,c:Crossing any street.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and in unmarked crosswalks at intersections. While you should always use caution around any pedestrian, the legal right‑of‑way specifically applies to pedestrians in crosswalks—marked or unmarked—at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.,c:Maintain your speed and quickly look both ways.
note: If buildings, parked cars, or other objects block your view at an intersection, stop first. Then slowly move forward until you can clearly see cross traffic in both directions. Enter the intersection only when you are sure it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Both when a police officer orders you to stop and at a red traffic light.,b:Only at a red traffic light.,c:Only when an officer orders you to stop.
note: You must stop for red traffic lights and stop signs, and you must also stop when a police officer or authorized person lawfully directs you to. Traffic signals and officers’ instructions both have to be obeyed.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what is the correct response?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to regain traction.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.,c:Speed up to get through the water faster.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. If this occurs, gently ease off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or turn suddenly, as that can cause a skid. Let the vehicle slow down gradually until the tires regain traction.

question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Turn wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Keep wheels pointing straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into traffic. Always set the parking brake and put the vehicle in park (or in gear for a manual transmission).

question: How should you behave when encountering a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the person is well away from your path of travel.,b:Carefully drive around them while they are crossing.,c:Sound your horn as you pass to alert them.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and has the right-of-way. You must stop and remain stopped until the person has completely crossed and is well clear of your path. Do not honk, rev the engine, or drive around them, as this can be confusing and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When completing a pass, when should you return to your previous lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.,b:When you sense you are far enough ahead of the other vehicle.,c:When the other driver signals for you to return.
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is enough space between you. This ensures you do not cut off the other driver and that you have a safe following distance.

question: Who may legally use marked handicap parking spaces?
options: a:Only drivers or passengers with the appropriate license plate or hanging placard.,b:Anyone when other spaces are full.,c:People who claim they do not feel well that day.
note: Marked handicap (accessible) parking spaces are reserved only for vehicles displaying a valid disability license plate or placard issued by the state, and only when the person with the disability is driving or being transported. Using these spaces without proper authorization is illegal and can result in fines.

question: What happens as your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases?
options: a:You become more coordinated.,b:You become more intoxicated and impaired.,c:You become more alert.,d:Your reaction times improve.
note: As your BAC goes up, alcohol affects your brain more. Your judgment, coordination, and reaction time all get worse, so you become more impaired and less able to drive safely.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what action may be necessary immediately?
options: a:Brake immediately and use a sharp blast of your horn to warn and stop the child.,b:Sound a sharp blast of your horn only, without slowing.,c:Start to prepare to slow down only.
note: If a child is about to run into the street, you must react immediately to prevent a collision. Brake at once and be prepared to stop, and use a sharp horn blast to warn the child and others. Never rely only on the horn; always slow or stop to avoid hitting a pedestrian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Change lanes or adjust your speed to create a safe gap for entering vehicles.,b:Maintain your speed and position at all times.,c:Honk at the entering drivers to make them wait.
note: When traffic is entering a freeway, help keep traffic flowing smoothly and safely by making room. If you can, change lanes away from the on‑ramp; if you cannot, adjust your speed so there is a safe gap for the entering vehicle to merge.

question: What color are temporary construction and maintenance warning devices?
options: a:Orange,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Temporary construction and maintenance warning devices, such as work zone signs, cones, and barrels, are orange. Orange tells drivers to expect workers, lane shifts, and other changes, and to slow down and use extra caution.

question: Blue roadway signs provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.
note: Blue signs are service signs. They point to motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals so drivers can find needed services while traveling.

question: Which headlights should you use in fog, heavy rain, or snow?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only without headlights.
note: In fog, heavy rain, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams and, if equipped, fog lights used together help you see the road and help others see you without excessive glare.

question: What term describes the amount of alcohol present in a person's bloodstream?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC),b:Implied consent (IC),c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC)
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the standard way to describe how much alcohol is in a person’s bloodstream. It is usually expressed as a percentage and is used by law enforcement to determine if a driver is legally impaired.

question: The driver in front of you has stopped at a crosswalk. What is your required action?
options: a:Cautiously pass at 10 mph or slower.,b:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have cleared.,c:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: If a driver has stopped at a crosswalk, you must not pass them. There may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see. You are required to stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have completely cleared the crosswalk and it is safe to go.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what steering action should you take?
options: a:Steer to the left,b:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral,c:Steer to the right,d:Pump the brakes rapidly
note: When the rear of your vehicle skids, you should ease off the pedals and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This helps you realign the vehicle with the direction of travel and regain control.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax, concentrate on driving, and be realistic about travel time.,b:Tailgate slow drivers to encourage them to speed up.,c:Drive above the posted limit to avoid delays.,d:Use gestures to communicate frustration.
note: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay relaxed, focus on safe driving, and allow enough time for your trip so you are not rushed. Obey speed limits, avoid tailgating or hostile gestures, and do not take other drivers’ mistakes personally.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Wait — allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink strong coffee to sober up quickly.,c:Take a cold shower to remove alcohol effects.
note: Time is the only thing that reduces your blood alcohol concentration. Your liver needs time to process alcohol, and nothing speeds this up—not coffee, cold showers, exercise, or food. Until enough time passes, you remain impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass a vehicle on the right by using the shoulder?
options: a:If the shoulder is paved and it's safe.,b:When the car ahead is driving too slowly.,c:Never drive off the pavement onto the shoulder to pass.,d:Whenever traffic is slow.
note: You must not drive off the paved roadway or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Passing on the right is allowed only when it can be done on a proper lane or paved portion of the roadway and is legal and safe—never by using the shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start into an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:No — never enter if you will block the intersection.,b:Only if you entered on a yellow light.,c:Only if you entered on a green light.,d:Yes, if you have the right-of-way.
note: You should only enter an intersection if you are sure you can clear it completely. Entering when traffic ahead is stopped can leave you blocking cross traffic when the light changes, which is illegal and unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and not already in it, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop if possible.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Maintain your speed and proceed through.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and stop if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up to try to beat the red light.

question: When you approach a stopped school bus with its lights flashing and arm extended, you should:
options: a:Stop.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.,c:Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped in most situations, even if you do not see children. Do not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: When is it legal to go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never — you must not go around or under any lowered gate.,b:When the lights are not flashing.,c:When you can see clearly in both directions.
note: You must never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. The gate, lights, and bells are there to warn you that a train is approaching or present. Even if you do not immediately see a train, another train may be coming or moving faster than you expect. Always wait until the lights stop flashing, the gate is fully raised, and the tracks are completely clear before crossing.

question: It is very foggy. What should you do with your lights?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Use high beam headlights.,c:Use low beam headlights.,d:Turn off all lights to avoid glare.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights so you can see and be seen without creating extra glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Never turn off your lights in fog; other drivers need to see you. Use low beams and, if your vehicle has them, fog lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into traffic from a curb or parked position, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a large enough gap so you can accelerate to the speed of traffic before merging.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet after merging.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass and then move into the lane.
note: When pulling away from a curb or parked position, you must wait for a gap that lets you accelerate up to the speed of traffic without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge only when you can safely match the flow. Do not move out just because a certain number of vehicles have passed; base your decision on an actual safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit in a school zone?
options: a:There is no single maximum school zone speed for all areas; obey the posted school zone speed limit signs.,b:School zones are always 15 mph in every state.,c:School zones are always 20 mph in every state.
note: School zone speed limits are set by each state and can vary; there is no single maximum speed that applies everywhere in the U.S. Common school zone limits include 15, 20, 25, or even 30 mph, and they may only apply at certain times or when lights are flashing. Always obey the specific posted school zone speed limit signs in your area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway you should:
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Always stop before entering the highway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed and find a safe gap in traffic. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge smoothly into the nearest lane at or near the speed of traffic. Do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and never try to cross multiple lanes at once when first entering.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Centerline separates opposing traffic,b:Do not pass,c:Reduce your speed,d:Traffic signal ahead
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not cross it to pass other vehicles. It marks a no‑passing zone for your direction of travel, usually because of limited visibility or other hazards.

question: How must you yield to an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive as close to the right edge and stop, taking care not to stop in an intersection.,b:Pull into the right lane and slow until it has passed.,c:Stop immediately even if you are in the middle of an intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must move as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Only when slowing down.,b:Often to monitor traffic behind you.,c:Only before changing lanes.,d:Never; mirrors distract you.
note: You should check your mirrors frequently—about every few seconds—to stay aware of traffic behind you. This helps you react early to fast‑approaching vehicles, tailgaters, or changing traffic conditions and is especially important before slowing, turning, or changing lanes.

question: When a school bus ahead is stopped with red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus cautiously.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This rule generally applies to traffic in both directions unless you are on a divided highway with a physical median and your state specifically exempts the opposite side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull completely off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and allow the passing vehicle to re-enter your lane safely.
note: If another driver is passing you, even in a no‑passing zone, focus on safety: maintain a steady path and, if needed, gently slow down to give them more room to return to the lane. Do not speed up or block the pass; your goal is to reduce the risk of a collision.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops directly in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop, even with good brakes. If you cut in front of them and then brake suddenly, the driver may not be able to stop in time, greatly increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: If the centerline is a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is on your side, what does that mean?
options: a:You may pass other vehicles to the left when it is safe.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You may only turn right.,d:You must merge immediately.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may cross it to pass another vehicle, but only when you have enough clear distance and it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into any available lane.,b:Into the first lane in the direction of travel.,c:Into the second lane from the curb.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the first lane available in the direction you are going. This keeps traffic organized, reduces conflicts with other vehicles, and makes it easier for others to predict your path.

question: If you see a person using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what is required of you?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield to traffic.,b:You must yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,c:Flash your headlights to warn them.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is visually impaired and has the right-of-way at crossings. You must stop or yield as needed, allow them to cross safely, and never honk or try to rush them. Wait until they are completely out of your path before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and find an alternate route.,b:Proceed to the next exit and return to your intended exit via surface streets.,c:Back up on the roadway or shoulder to reach the missed exit.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, you must continue to the next exit. Backing up on the freeway or shoulder is extremely dangerous and illegal in most places because traffic is moving at high speeds and drivers do not expect a vehicle reversing.

question: How are bicycles treated when using the roadway?
options: a:Are considered vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,b:Do not follow specific rules of the road.,c:Must always yield the right-of-way to motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles on the roadway are generally treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of motor vehicles, and they are entitled to use the road and be given the same respect and space.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels toward the curb or side of the road.,b:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep the wheels straight.,d:Turn the wheels toward traffic flow.
note: When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or road edge and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will rest against the curb or edge instead of rolling into traffic.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow on a traffic signal signify?
options: a:Drivers should immediately stop and remain stopped.,b:The protected left turn is ending and you should prepare to yield.,c:The left turn will remain protected indefinitely.
note: A yellow left‑turn arrow means the protected left‑turn phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe, and when the signal changes you must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You — the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. If you are on the right, you may proceed first after stopping and ensuring it is safe.

question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,b:Never; always assert your right-of-way.,c:Often even at controlled intersections.,d:Only to emergency vehicles.
note: Right‑of‑way is not something you "take"; it is something others give you. You should always be prepared to yield your legal right‑of‑way whenever doing so can prevent a collision, even if you technically have the priority.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What important step must you take before passing on a two-lane road?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles to ensure safe clearance.,b:Sound your horn continuously.,c:Flash headlights at the vehicle ahead.,d:Pass without checking mirrors.
note: Before passing on a two-lane, two‑way road, you must be sure you have enough time and space to complete the pass without interfering with oncoming traffic or the vehicle you are passing. That means carefully judging the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles and ensuring you can return to your lane safely.

question: What color are most regulatory traffic signs?
options: a:White,b:Green,c:Yellow
note: Most regulatory signs, such as speed limit, no parking, and turn restrictions, are white rectangles with black or red lettering or symbols. The white background indicates a law or regulation that drivers must obey.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, the safest place for children age 12 and under is:
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: In vehicles with airbags, children age 12 and under are safest in the back seat. Front airbags deploy with great force and can seriously injure smaller passengers, so children should ride properly restrained in the rear seats.

question: When an oncoming vehicle has bright headlights at night, how should you avoid being blinded?
options: a:Stop until the vehicle passes.,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look directly at the oncoming headlights.,d:Flash your high beams.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s high beams are too bright at night, you should avoid looking directly at the lights. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road while still keeping track of your lane position. This reduces glare and helps you maintain control.

question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection and wait.,b:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,c:Pull to the right side of the intersection and stop.,d:Speed up and get out of the way.
note: If you are already in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you should continue through the intersection first. Once you have cleared it, pull to the right side of the road and stop. This keeps the intersection from becoming blocked and allows the emergency vehicle a clear path.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can affect a driver's:
options: a:Knowledge of traffic laws.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Right-of-way privileges only.
note: Alcohol affects the brain’s ability to think clearly and control muscles. Even a small amount can reduce judgment, slow reaction time, and weaken coordination, which makes it harder to steer, brake, and respond to hazards safely.

question: How can you avoid losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Slow down.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.,d:Use cruise control.
note: On wet roads, tires can lose contact with the pavement and start to ride on a thin layer of water, a condition called hydroplaning. Slowing down is the best way to maintain traction because it allows your tires to channel water away and stay in contact with the road.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is broken, drivers in either direction may pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Applying your brakes when possible.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Pressing your head against the head restraint.
note: If you are about to be hit from behind, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel so you can control the vehicle and avoid being pushed into another lane or vehicle. Press your head back against the head restraint to reduce whiplash, and be ready to brake to prevent a secondary collision.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what is the safest action before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down and cool off before you drive.,b:Loudly play the radio while driving to distract yourself.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions like anger can distract you, narrow your focus, and lead to aggressive driving decisions. The safest choice is to wait and calm down before driving so you can concentrate fully on the road and other users.

question: What speed should you choose relative to road and weather conditions?
options: a:A speed appropriate for the current road and weather conditions.,b:Always at the posted speed limit.,c:Always at the speed of surrounding vehicles.
note: You must always choose a speed that is safe for current conditions, even if that means driving below the posted limit. Factors like rain, fog, ice, heavy traffic, and poor visibility require you to slow down. However, you may never legally exceed the posted speed limit, even if conditions seem ideal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:The speed you drive does not affect safety.
