note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake suddenly, change lanes abruptly, or attempt risky passing maneuvers. On many highways, you are required to keep up with the reasonable flow of traffic (within the speed limit) or use the right lane if you must drive more slowly.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at a crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,b:Look for a second train.,c:Both of the above.
note: After a train passes, you must not proceed until all warning devices (lights, gates, bells) have stopped and the gates are fully raised. You must also look and listen carefully for a second train coming from either direction before crossing, because another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: At a flashing red traffic signal, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light stops flashing.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line or before entering the intersection, yield to pedestrians and other vehicles with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You must stay within your lane,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane,d:You may cross only to pass large vehicles
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as what?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither a stimulant nor depressant.,d:A performance enhancer.
note: Alcohol acts as a central nervous system depressant. Even in low concentrations, it slows brain activity, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment and reaction time, which makes driving dangerous.

question: How does excessive speed affect crash severity?
options: a:It increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.,b:It saves time and usually improves safety.,c:It helps you maneuver around obstacles more easily.
note: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the greater the force of any impact. This means crashes at higher speeds are more likely to cause serious injury or death, even if the difference in speed seems small.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren is approaching you, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving but stay out of its path.,b:Pull over toward the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stopping. If you are in an intersection, first clear the intersection, then pull over and stop so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: If driving on a highway next to a single broken white line, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:Cross the line to pass or change lanes when safe.,b:Never cross the line.,c:Cross only to make right turns.,d:Cross only during daytime.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you return to your original lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you have enough space ahead of the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror before returning to the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass a vehicle on the road?
options: a:When a solid center line is next to your lane.,b:When there is a broken center line next to your lane.,c:On a hill or curve where you cannot see ahead.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe and legal to do so. You must not pass where there is a solid line next to your lane or where your view ahead is blocked, such as on hills, curves, or near intersections.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, braking can make the skid worse. Take your foot off the accelerator, stay off the brakes, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle is back under control, you may brake gently if needed.

question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,b:You signal your intention for three seconds.,c:You can see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the headlights (or front of the vehicle) you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space and will not cut off the other driver.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, which lights should be used?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beams.,c:Parking lights.,d:Interior dome lights.
note: In rain or fog, always use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road while making your vehicle more visible to others. High beams reflect off moisture and fog, making it harder to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed and hope traffic clears quickly.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.,c:Turn left to find another route immediately.
note: Even with a green light, you must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it. Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead moves so you do not block cross traffic or cause gridlock.

question: What does a red arrow pointing to the right mean?
options: a:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped for that movement. You may not turn in the direction of the red arrow until it changes to green or a green arrow appears.

question: What does an orange-and-red triangular emblem on the back of a slow vehicle mean?
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle and travels at lower speeds.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:There is shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange-and-red reflective triangle on the rear of a vehicle is the slow-moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, so you should be prepared to slow down.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a small passenger car,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle,including large trucks,buses,or vehicles towing trailers,c:When following a station wagon,d:When following a motorcycle
note: You should allow extra following distance behind large vehicles or any driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle, such as trucks, buses, or vehicles towing trailers. These drivers may not see you in their mirrors, and they need more time and space to stop or maneuver, so you should stay farther back to give yourself a better view and more reaction time.

question: What do yellow centerlines on the road mark?
options: a:The separation of traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Carpool lanes separated from regular lanes.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. Crossing these lines is only allowed when passing is permitted and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and always has the right-of-way. You must stop or yield as needed and use extra caution, regardless of whether a crossing guard is present.

question: If another driver is acting aggressively toward you, how should you respond?
options: a:Get out of their way and avoid confrontation.,b:Challenge them to establish right-of-way.,c:Speed up to put distance between you immediately.
note: If another driver is aggressive, do not respond or escalate. Stay calm, avoid eye contact, and safely move out of their way by changing lanes or slowing so they can pass. Your goal is to create space and reduce the chance of a confrontation or crash.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers only.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams, and fog lights if equipped, help you see the road and help others see you without creating glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: What is the correct mindset when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and drive with extra caution.,b:Slightly increase your speed to clear the zone.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.,d:Ignore signs and maintain your normal driving.
note: In construction zones, expect the unexpected: lane shifts, workers close to traffic, equipment entering the roadway, and sudden stops. Slow down, obey all signs and flaggers, and increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react safely.

question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:
options: a:Help you to be a better driver.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness affects your brain much like alcohol: it slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment. A tired driver may not notice hazards or may react too slowly, greatly increasing the risk of a crash.

question: Collisions are more likely when which condition exists?
options: a:All vehicles travel at about the same speed.,b:One vehicle travels much faster or slower than surrounding traffic.,c:Everyone follows the flow of traffic.,d:Weather is perfect.
note: A vehicle moving much faster or slower than surrounding traffic forces others to brake, change lanes, or accelerate unexpectedly, which increases the chance of collisions. When most vehicles travel at about the same speed, traffic flow is smoother and safer.

question: On the freeway behind a large truck, how should you follow?
options: a:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,c:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and have large blind spots directly in front, behind, and along the sides. Following farther behind gives you better visibility around the truck and more time to react if it slows or stops suddenly.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on highways?
options: a:They separate lanes of traffic traveling in opposite directions and indicate passing is permitted.,b:They separate lanes moving in the same direction.,c:They indicate no passing zones.,d:They mark the road edge.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the yellow line is broken (dashed), it means you may pass another vehicle if it is safe and legal to do so. Solid yellow lines generally indicate no passing.

question: How is a crosswalk defined?
options: a:A type of four-way intersection.,b:An area set aside for road workers.,c:An area designated for pedestrian crossing of the roadway.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross. It may be marked with painted lines or be unmarked at an intersection where sidewalks meet the street corners.

question: Which of the following is true about impairment from alcohol and drugs?
options: a:They only affect alertness and concentration.,b:They only affect reaction time and coordination.,c:They affect alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect the central nervous system and can reduce alertness, harm concentration, slow reaction time, and weaken coordination. Because safe driving depends on all of these abilities, any such impairment increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds have passed.,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: On a two-lane road, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and have checked your blind spot. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to make the rider move to the shoulder,b:Remain in the same lane because the motorcycle is small,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass,d:Pass using only part of the motorcycle's lane
note: Motorcycles need a full lane just like any other vehicle. When passing, move completely into the left lane, pass safely, and do not crowd or share the motorcycle’s lane. Return to your lane only when you can do so without cutting the rider off.

question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:
options: a:Closer to the car ahead than normal.,b:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c:No different than normal.
note: On slippery roads, it takes longer to stop, so you must increase your following distance. Leaving more space gives you extra time to brake gently and avoid skidding if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Slow enough to stop within the area your headlights illuminate.,b:Turn on high beams to better see ahead.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to others.
note: At night on dimly lit roads, you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called not overdriving your headlights and helps you react in time to hazards that appear in the lit area.

question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Reduce your speed to a safe level for the curve.,b:Activate your turn signal before the curve.,c:Brake hard as you enter the curve.
note: Before entering a curve, slow down to a safe speed while the vehicle is still straight. Braking hard in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, so most of your speed reduction should happen before you begin turning.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a clearly written note with your name, address, and contact information securely attached to the vehicle. You are also required to report the collision to law enforcement if the damage meets your state’s reporting threshold.

question: Which lights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Fog lights,b:Low beam headlights,c:Parking lights,d:High beam headlights
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light pattern aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, you may use them together with low beams, but never use only parking lights while moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed repeatedly on the right and left while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the center lane regardless.,b:Move to the lane on your right when safe.,c:Move to the lane on your left immediately.
note: On multi-lane highways, slower traffic should generally use the right lane. If you are in the center lane and vehicles are passing you on both sides, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic. When it is safe, move to the lane on your right so faster traffic can pass on the left as intended.

question: What is the purpose of barriers, drums, cones, and signs in a work zone?
options: a:To annoy drivers with slow traffic.,b:To inconvenience travelers.,c:To keep traffic away from hazardous work areas and protect workers.
note: Barriers, drums, cones, and signs in work zones are used to guide and separate traffic from workers and hazardous areas. They help you see lane shifts, closed lanes, and work activity so you can slow down, follow the path indicated, and protect both yourself and road workers.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts together.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: A two-part safety belt is designed to be used as a system. The lap belt should be worn low and snug across your hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the center of your chest and shoulder, not your neck or under your arm. Using both together keeps you from sliding under the belt and reduces the risk of serious injury in a crash.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Another vehicle is in your way.,b:When it may help prevent a collision.,c:Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to a potential collision or dangerous situation. Do not use it because you are annoyed, blocked in traffic, or to punish another driver’s mistake.

question: How can sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:They only affect large vehicles.,b:They can create problems for all vehicles.,c:They only cause visibility problems.,d:They have no impact on vehicle control.
note: Strong or sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways and affect steering and stability, especially at highway speeds. All drivers should be prepared to adjust steering and speed when winds are strong.

question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many drugs—illegal, prescription, and over‑the‑counter—can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect judgment. Always read labels and avoid driving if a medication can cause drowsiness or impaired alertness.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams at night, how should you respond?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane and watch the vehicle from the corner of your eye.,b:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Keep looking straight ahead in your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to track the other vehicle until it passes.

question: Which of these is a recommended safe driving habit?
options: a:Using high beams in fog.,b:Checking rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Staring constantly at the road ahead.,d:Driving without signaling.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan all around: ahead, to the sides, and behind. Checking your mirrors every few seconds helps you spot vehicles approaching quickly, changing lanes, or following too closely so you can react early.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another car?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; it is unsafe and illegal in most situations.

question: What should you expect about traction when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires have less traction than on pavement so you must slow down,b:Visibility is better on gravel and dirt roads,c:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement,d:You can stop more quickly on dirt surfaces
note: Loose gravel and dirt provide much less traction than paved roads. Your tires are more likely to slide, and it takes longer to stop. You should slow down, increase following distance, and avoid sudden steering, acceleration, or braking on these surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's direction and go through without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,d:Ignore the officer and obey the signal.
note: A police officer’s directions always override traffic signals and signs. If an officer clearly directs you to proceed through a red light, you must follow their instructions, moving carefully as directed while still watching for other road users.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you must actively scan to the left and right for pedestrians, cyclists, trains, and cross traffic. Looking to the sides helps you spot hazards early so you can slow or stop in time, even when your light is green.

question: When driving on snow or ice, which practice helps prevent skidding on steep downgrades?
options: a:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.,b:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.,c:Maintain a close following distance to the vehicle ahead.
note: On snow or ice, using a low gear before going down a steep hill helps the engine slow the vehicle so you rely less on the brakes. This reduces the chance of your wheels locking and the vehicle skidding. You should also increase following distance and brake gently and early on slippery downgrades.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. If you drive next to them for a long time, the driver may not see you and could change lanes into your path. Safest practice is to avoid lingering beside large vehicles: either pass promptly and safely or drop back so you are clearly visible.

question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Slow down and drive at a reduced speed for the conditions.,b:Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.,c:Apply the brakes as soon as the car begins to skid.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, causing loss of steering and braking control. The best prevention is to slow down in wet conditions so your tires can push water aside and maintain grip. Adjust your speed to the weather, use proper tire inflation and tread, and avoid sudden braking or sharp turns on wet roads.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must present proof of financial responsibility (insurance) to an officer after a traffic stop or collision when requested.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and siren, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling over to the right edge or curb of the road and stopping until it has passed. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can move quickly and safely. Only proceed once it has gone by and it is safe and legal to continue.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates that passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line may not pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, so always check carefully for oncoming vehicles before passing.

question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:When the other driver signals you to return.
note: After you pass another vehicle, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the front of the vehicle (or its headlights at night) clearly in your inside rearview mirror. This helps ensure you have enough space and are not cutting the other driver off. Always signal and check your blind spot before returning to the lane.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,b:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:Alcohol affects judgement, which is needed to drive safely.
note: Alcohol affects judgment, reaction time, and coordination even at low blood alcohol levels, well before you feel drunk. Because safe driving depends heavily on good judgment and quick decisions, any amount of alcohol can impair your ability to drive safely, even if you are under the legal limit.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.,b:Reduce your speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.
note: When heavy smoke or similar visibility hazards cover the roadway, you should slow down, move as far to the right as you can, and pull completely off the roadway if possible. Turn on your hazard lights so others can see you, and wait until visibility improves before continuing. Driving into thick smoke at normal speed is extremely dangerous because you may not see stopped vehicles or obstacles ahead.

question: Because motorcycles and mopeds are harder to see, what should motorists do?
options: a:Share the lane with them.,b:Make frequent visual checks and be alert.,c:Drive faster to pass them quickly.,d:Ignore small vehicles in traffic.
note: Motorcycles and mopeds are smaller and can be easily hidden in blind spots or behind other vehicles. Drivers should make frequent visual checks, including checking mirrors and turning their head to check blind spots before changing lanes or turning. Give motorcycles a full lane and extra following distance, and never try to share a lane with them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what conditions may you proceed on a red light when a green arrow is also displayed?
options: a:You may proceed in any direction if you are in the proper lane and the way is clear.,b:You may proceed straight only after coming to a full stop.,c:You may proceed straight only after the arrow turns off.,d:You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow; the red light still prohibits other movements.
note: A steady red light means you must stop and cannot proceed straight or turn in the direction controlled by that red signal. A green arrow allows you to move only in the direction of the arrow and only if you are in the proper lane and the way is clear. You may not proceed on the red for any other movement; the red still prohibits travel in directions not covered by the green arrow.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they lift and the tracks are clear.,b:Slow down and proceed if you think no train is coming.,c:Drive around the gates if you cannot see a train.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop and stay stopped well behind the gate. Never drive around or under the gates, even if you do not see a train. Wait until the lights stop flashing, the gates are fully raised, and you can clearly see that all tracks are clear before proceeding.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Driving aggressively to assert the right-of-way.,b:Using safe strategies to prevent crashes.,c:Driving more dangerously than other drivers.
note: Defensive driving means using safe, proactive strategies to avoid crashes. You stay alert, watch other road users, anticipate possible hazards, and adjust your speed and position so you have time and space to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: When passing, you should move into the passing lane only when it is legal and clear, then pass the other vehicle promptly without exceeding the speed limit. Passing safely and efficiently reduces the time you spend in the opposing lane or in another driver’s blind spot. Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your mirror and it is safe.

question: What is the definition of distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from the driving task. This includes taking your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving, such as texting, eating, or adjusting controls while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic before merging?
options: a:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to check blind spots, then merge when safe.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use rearview and side mirrors but do not look over your shoulder.
note: When entering a freeway, use your mirrors to judge traffic and then make a quick glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before merging. This combination ensures you see vehicles that may not appear in your mirrors so you can merge smoothly and safely into the flow of traffic.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:Loading zone.,b:No parking, standing, or stopping.,c:Passenger pick-up/drop-off only.,d:Emergency parking only.
note: A red-painted curb means you may not stop, stand, or park there for any reason, except when required to obey a traffic control device or officer. It is used to keep areas completely clear for safety or traffic flow.

question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:The same as a yield sign.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently if needed.,b:Turn the front wheels sharply to re-enter the pavement.,c:Apply the brakes hard immediately and stop.,d:Accelerate quickly and then steer back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently if needed to slow down. Once you have the vehicle under control and your speed is reduced, check for traffic and gently steer back onto the pavement. Avoid jerking the wheel or braking hard, as that can cause you to lose control.

question: A driver's license is considered which of the following?
options: a:A privilege, not a right.,b:A right, not a privilege.,c:A requirement.
note: A driver’s license is a privilege granted by the state, not an automatic right. You must meet legal requirements to obtain it, and it can be suspended or revoked if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, how fast should you be driving?
options: a:At or near the speed of freeway traffic.,b:Much slower than the freeway traffic.,c:At a speed significantly above the posted limit.,d:At any comfortable speed.
note: When using a freeway on-ramp, you should use the acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near that of traffic already on the freeway, without exceeding the speed limit. Matching the flow of traffic makes it easier and safer to merge.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking coffee,b:Time,c:Taking a cold shower,d:Eating fatty foods
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol. Nothing else reliably speeds up the process.

question: What is the correct response to a tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Slow down gradually and apply the brakes lightly.,c:Brake hard immediately and steer to shoulder.
note: In a tire blowout, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once you have good control and your speed has dropped, apply the brakes lightly and steer to a safe place off the road. Hard or sudden braking can cause loss of control.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Judgment,b:Vision,c:Balance
note: Alcohol first affects judgment and decision-making. Even at low BAC levels, people become less cautious, take more risks, and misjudge situations. This poor judgment then leads to unsafe choices that affect steering, speed control, and reaction to hazards.

question: If someone is following you too closely on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.,c:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.
note: When someone is following too closely and you cannot change lanes, gradually reduce your speed to increase your following distance ahead and encourage the tailgater to pass when it is safe. Avoid sudden braking or speeding up, as both can increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what should you do?
options: a:Turn around and seek an alternate route — do not attempt to drive through the water.,b:Slam on the brakes to avoid the water.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway across the flooded area.
note: If the road ahead is flooded, turn around and find another route. Even shallow water can cause you to lose control or stall, and deeper water can sweep your vehicle away or hide road damage. It is never safe to drive through floodwater.

question: What must drivers do when a school bus is loading or unloading children?
options: a:Stop completely when the bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus, even on undivided roads.,c:Slow down and be ready to stop.
note: You must stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended when approaching from either direction on an undivided road. On a divided highway with a physical median, only the traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; oncoming traffic on the other side of the median may proceed with caution.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your ability to see other vehicles, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on parking lights and continue at normal speed.,b:Turn on emergency flashers only.,c:Slow down and turn on your headlights.
note: When dust or smoke reduces visibility, slow down so you have more time to react and turn on your headlights (low beams) so other drivers can see you. Parking lights or emergency flashers alone do not provide adequate visibility or meet legal requirements in low-visibility conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and check mirrors and blind spots.,b:Assume other drivers will make space for you.,c:Only check your inside rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, always signal to show your intention, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never assume others will move for you; you must be sure the lane is clear before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not working?
options: a:Treat it as an all-way stop: come to a complete stop and yield before entering.,b:Proceed without stopping if the intersection looks clear.,c:Drive through quickly to avoid delaying traffic.,d:Follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.
note: If a traffic signal is completely out, treat the intersection like an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed only after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians who arrived first or are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps decide who goes first when arrival is simultaneous.

question: When a stopped school bus ahead of you on your side of the road has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and pass cautiously.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,d:Proceed if no children are visible.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must come to a complete stop and stay stopped. The flashing red lights mean children are getting on or off the bus and may be crossing the road. You may not move again until the red lights stop flashing and the bus starts moving or the driver signals that it is safe to proceed.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Find a safe place to stop and take a break or nap.,b:Try to fight it and continue driving.,c:Take caffeine pills and keep driving.
note: If you feel drowsy while driving, you must get off the road as soon as it is safe and rest or switch drivers. Drowsiness seriously slows your reaction time and judgment, and trying to fight it with willpower or stimulants is unsafe. The only safe response is to stop driving until you are fully alert again.

question: What should you do when you see a deep puddle on the roadway?
options: a:Maintain posted speed to get through it.,b:Avoid the puddle if possible.,c:Shift into neutral while crossing.,d:Brake hard just before entering.
note: If you see a deep puddle ahead, the safest choice is to avoid it if you can do so safely. Deep water can cause hydroplaning, loss of control, or damage to your brakes, engine, or electrical systems. If you cannot avoid it, slow down before entering and drive through at a steady, reduced speed without sudden braking or steering.

question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Before you start the vehicle, you should always fasten your own seat belt and make sure all passengers are properly buckled. Making this a habit every time you drive greatly reduces the risk of serious injury in a crash and ensures everyone in the vehicle is using their restraints correctly.

question: When parking on a hill, what is the correct action to take?
options: a:Turn the front wheels so the vehicle would roll into the curb or away from traffic if the brakes fail,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear for a manual),c:Both a and b,d:Leave the transmission in neutral and do not set the parking brake
note: When parking on a hill, always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear with a manual transmission) so it cannot roll. In addition, turn the front wheels so that if the vehicle does move, it will roll into the curb or away from traffic: uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb; downhill or uphill with no curb, turn wheels toward the edge of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is NOT a safe practice on an interstate highway?
options: a:Change lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.
note: On interstates, you must always signal before changing lanes so other drivers know your intentions. If you miss your exit, you must continue to the next exit; never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the interstate because that is extremely dangerous and illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal before changing lanes,b:Never attempt to pass or otherwise change lanes in an intersection,c:Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder,d:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane
note: You should never pass or change lanes within an intersection because traffic and pedestrians can enter from many directions and conditions can change quickly. When changing lanes, you must signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and also be aware of other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars going straight.,c:No one — they have the right-of-way.,d:Cars behind them.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, because they have the right‑of‑way. You may only complete your left turn when it is safe and there is a sufficient gap in oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, what should you check?
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: As you prepare to stop for a traffic signal or sign, check your mirrors for traffic behind and around you. This helps you slow and stop smoothly, gives drivers behind you time to react, and lets you adjust if someone is approaching too fast.

question: What must vehicles do at a crosswalk?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians who have the right-of-way.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles.,c:Require construction workers to yield to vehicular traffic.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks when they have the right‑of‑way, stopping if necessary to let them cross safely. You should never expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles; drivers bear the primary responsibility to avoid collisions.

question: What is the best way to check a blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Use your side mirror only.,c:Rely on the inside rearview mirror only.
note: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, you must quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder into the lane you want to enter. Mirrors alone are not enough to see vehicles in your blind spots.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Stop completely and wait four seconds.,b:Yield to all traffic before entering.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, be prepared to yield, and proceed only when it is safe. You must watch carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians and yield if they are already in or close to the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Cutting the corner short and interfering with other traffic.,b:Slowing down as you approach the turn.,c:Using your turn signal to alert others.
note: When turning left, you must stay in your lane and turn into the correct lane without cutting across the corner or into opposing or adjacent traffic. Cutting the corner can put you into the path of oncoming vehicles or vehicles turning beside you. Always signal and slow down before the turn so you can turn smoothly and safely.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal indicate for drivers preparing to turn?
options: a:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,b:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,c:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending and the signal will soon change to red. You should prepare to stop if you have not yet entered the intersection, and you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: With oncoming traffic to your left and parked cars to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming vehicles and parked cars.,b:Stay as close to parked vehicles as possible.,c:Move closer to oncoming traffic to give parked vehicles room.
note: When there are hazards on both sides—oncoming traffic to the left and parked cars to the right—position your vehicle near the center of your lane. This gives you the most space from both dangers and allows more time to react if a door opens or a vehicle drifts toward the center line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection at the posted speed when the light turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Ignore the signal and proceed normally.,d:Honk and proceed.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you can safely stop before entering the intersection, you must do so. If stopping suddenly would cause a rear‑end collision or you are already too close to stop safely, continue through the intersection with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does safe interstate driving require?
options: a:The ability to safely drive at increased speeds and constant alertness.,b:Only knowing where exits are.,c:Constantly using cruise control.,d:Only being able to drive at the posted speed limit.
note: Safe interstate driving requires staying alert for long periods and being able to control your vehicle smoothly at higher speeds. You must scan far ahead, check mirrors frequently, adjust speed to traffic and weather, and leave extra following distance because stopping distances increase at freeway speeds.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along road edges or centerlines?
options: a:To alert inattentive drivers through vibration and sound.,b:To test vehicle tire condition.,c:To mark pedestrian crossings.,d:To slow traffic like speed bumps.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the pavement that cause noise and vibration when you drive over them. They are designed to alert inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, giving them time to correct their path.

question: Which statement about driving through roadwork zones is true?
options: a:Fines are often higher in work zones and you must obey posted work‑zone limits.,b:You must slow down and obey all signs and flaggers in the Cone Zone.,c:You must slow down even if no workers are visible.
note: Work zones often have reduced speed limits and narrowed or shifted lanes. You must slow down and obey all work‑zone signs and flaggers, even if you do not see workers present. Lower speeds give you more time to react to lane changes, equipment, and workers, and fines are often increased in these areas.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and proceed with caution.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane without checking traffic.
note: Animals near the roadway can suddenly move into your path. You should slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop. Do not speed up or swerve suddenly, because you could lose control or collide with another vehicle. Reducing speed and proceeding cautiously gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: Which factor affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed by a person?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: A person’s weight is one of several factors that affect how quickly alcohol is absorbed and how it impacts blood alcohol concentration. Generally, a smaller person will reach a higher BAC than a larger person after drinking the same amount. Other important factors include sex, how much and how recently the person has eaten, and how much and how quickly alcohol is consumed.

question: How do stopping distance and severity of collisions change with vehicle speed?
options: a:They decrease as speed increases.,b:They are unaffected by speed.,c:They increase as speed increases.
note: As speed increases, both stopping distance and crash severity increase. At higher speeds, your vehicle needs more distance to come to a complete stop because both reaction distance and braking distance grow. In a collision, the force of impact rises sharply with speed, making injuries and damage more severe.

question: At what speed can a car begin to hydroplane in standing water?
options: a:35 miles per hour,b:45 miles per hour,c:40 miles per hour
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds as low as about 35 mph when there is enough standing water and your tires cannot channel it away. At that point, your tires may ride up on a thin film of water, reducing or even eliminating contact with the road and causing a loss of steering and braking control. Slowing down in wet conditions greatly reduces this risk.

question: How are bicycles treated when used on roadways?
options: a:As vehicles subject to the same rules.,b:As hazards that must be avoided at all costs.,c:As pedestrians.,d:As vehicles that always have the right-of-way.
note: When bicycles are used on the roadway, they are generally treated as vehicles. Bicyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of motor vehicles. Drivers must also share the road safely with bicycles, giving them space and yielding when required, but bicycles do not automatically have the right‑of‑way in every situation.

question: How should you respond at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped while the light is red regardless of conditions.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any pedestrians and other vehicles that have the right‑of‑way, then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.,b:Toward the center of the roadway.,c:Straight ahead in your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, the bright light can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, shift your gaze toward the right edge of your lane and use the white line or road edge as a guide while using your peripheral vision to monitor the other vehicle until it passes.

question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?
options: a:Even over-the-counter medicines can impair your driving.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:All prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Many legal medications, including common over‑the‑counter drugs like cold or allergy medicine, can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reactions. These effects can seriously impair your driving even if the drug is not illegal. Always read labels and warnings and talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving after taking any medication.

question: When driving at night, what should you remember?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra room to stop or steer away from hazards you may not see until later. Use high beams only when there is no oncoming traffic and no vehicle directly ahead of you, and avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights to prevent glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing,c:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings indicate it is allowed and where you have enough clear distance to complete the pass without interfering with oncoming traffic. Solid lines, no‑passing zone signs, hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings are typical places where passing is prohibited because your view or space is limited.

question: When driving at night you should:
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Driving at night reduces how far you can see and how quickly you can spot hazards. Increasing your following distance gives you more time to react and stop safely. Use your high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle, and avoid staring directly into other vehicles’ headlights to prevent glare.

question: When are headlights required by Mississippi law?
options: a:Between sunset and sunrise.,b:When the temperature drops below freezing.,c:When you are tired.,d:Only during snowstorms.
note: Mississippi law requires headlights to be used from sunset to sunrise and any time you cannot clearly see people or vehicles 500 feet ahead. Using low beams when you are within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle (and dimming high beams when following another vehicle within about 200–300 feet) prevents glare and helps everyone see the road safely.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while driving on the highway helps to:
options: a:Helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Scanning far ahead enables smoother driving, fewer sudden maneuvers, and better reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about changing lanes is correct?
options: a:You only need to look over your shoulder for left lane changes.,b:Look over the shoulder corresponding to the direction of the lane change to check blind spots.,c:If you have two outside mirrors, you have no blind spots.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and look over the left or right shoulder as appropriate to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you creating a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal,b:Honk and apply the brakes firmly,c:Swerve into the lane next to you,d:Speed up to pass the vehicle
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator to increase space between you and the other vehicle; avoid sudden braking or swerving unless necessary.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:In the rightmost travel lane.,b:With all four wheels off the main-traveled portion of the highway.,c:Where you stopped and leave the hazard lights off.,d:Facing oncoming traffic.
note: If your car is disabled, park with all wheels off the main-traveled roadway when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals override traffic lights and signs. Even if the signal is green, you must follow the officer’s command to stop or go, because they may be managing a hazard, collision, or special situation you cannot yet see.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you in a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in lane and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Drive to the right edge and slow down but remain moving.,d:Ignore it and keep driving.
note: On city streets, when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches from behind, you must move as far to the right as safely possible and stop until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop so the emergency vehicle has a clear path.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left (in the direction of the skid) to correct it.,b:Turn the steering wheel to the right to counter the skid.,c:Do not turn the steering wheel at all.
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, you should steer left—into the direction of the skid. This helps realign the front wheels with the direction the vehicle is sliding so the tires can regain traction. Avoid overcorrecting or jerking the wheel; make smooth steering and ease off the accelerator.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the traffic light is also working, whose directions should you follow?
options: a:The directions of the traffic light.,b:The officer's directions.,c:Ignore both and proceed cautiously.
note: A police officer’s directions always override traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. If an officer is directing traffic at a working signal, follow the officer, not the light, because they may be controlling traffic for a crash, road work, or special event.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which of the following is true?
options: a:They may use the left lane when it is safe and legal to prepare for a left turn.,b:They may also use a two-stage left turn from the right side where permitted.,c:They may cut through all lanes without yielding or signaling.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and duties as drivers. When making a left turn, a bicyclist may move into the appropriate left-turn lane or left side of the lane, just like a car, when it is safe. They may also use a two-stage turn from the right side in some situations, but they are never allowed to weave unpredictably or “cut through” lanes without yielding and signaling.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean for passing?
options: a:No passing is allowed from either direction.,b:Passing allowed from both directions.,c:Passing allowed only from your direction.,d:Passing allowed at certain times of day.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you reduce your speed?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately after entering the deceleration lane.
note: On an interstate, you should stay at highway speed until you reach the deceleration lane for your exit. Once you are fully in the deceleration lane, then begin slowing to the posted advisory speed for the ramp. Slowing on the main travel lanes can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: What is the only reliable way to lower your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Give your body time to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink strong coffee to sober up quickly.,c:Take a cold shower to become alert.
note: The only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is to give your body time to process the alcohol. Coffee, cold showers, exercise, or other tricks may make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how quickly your liver removes alcohol from your bloodstream.

question: When you approach a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.,b:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light stops flashing.
note: A flashing red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any pedestrians and other vehicles in or approaching the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: Which statement about driving and medications is accurate?
options: a:Many cold medicines and other over-the-counter drugs can cause drowsiness and impair driving.,b:Over-the-counter medicines cannot impair driving if taken as directed.,c:If a doctor prescribes a medication, it is always safe to drive while using it.
note: Many prescription and over-the-counter medicines, including some cold and allergy drugs, can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Always read the label and warnings, and talk with your doctor or pharmacist before driving when you start a new medication.

question: What does a solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line indicate?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe; vehicles next to the solid line may not.,b:Traffic in both directions may pass freely.,c:Only the lane next to the solid line may pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means only the traffic on the side with the broken line may pass, and only when it is safe. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even one drink can impair your driving ability enough to increase your crash risk, so you should never assume a small amount is safe for driving.

question: When passing a row of parked cars, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Someone or something unexpectedly entering your lane.,b:All pedestrians to wait for you.,c:To drive very close to the parked cars to allow traffic flow.,d:Parked cars to always stay put.
note: When passing parked cars, you must anticipate that a door may open, a person may step out, or a vehicle may pull out suddenly. Leave extra space when possible and be ready to slow or stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on a red light after stopping?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street, and no sign prohibits the turn,b:When traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street,c:Whenever you yield to all other traffic,d:Only if there is a posted sign allowing it
note: In many U.S. states, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, you may turn left on a red light only when turning from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, unless a sign specifically prohibits it. You may not turn left on red from or onto a two‑way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach a roundabout, you should slow down and do what?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians only.,b:Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout only.,c:Yield to both pedestrians and vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: As you approach a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks, and to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap in traffic.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline on your side of the road mean?
options: a:You may cross the line to pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:A construction zone is ahead.
note: A broken yellow line on your side means you may cross it to pass another vehicle, but only when you can see that the road ahead is clear and it is safe and legal to do so. If oncoming traffic is too close, visibility is poor, or a no‑passing zone begins, you must not pass.

question: A driver's license is considered what under the law?
options: a:A mandatory requirement.,b:A privilege granted by the state.,c:A constitutional right.
note: In all U.S. states, driving is a privilege, not a constitutional right. The state issues a driver’s license if you meet the requirements, and it can suspend or revoke that license for unsafe or illegal driving behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving into a gap in highway traffic, what should you do first?
options: a:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead to judge the gap.,b:Speed up and force other vehicles to make room.,c:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
note: When merging into highway traffic, you must first check behind and to the side using your mirrors and blind-spot checks. Once you know it is clear, you then adjust your speed to fit smoothly into a safe gap without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and keep passing, what is the likely result?
options: a:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely,b:Increase your chances of a collision,c:Help prevent traffic congestion,d:Improve fuel efficiency
note: Frequently passing on a two‑lane road puts you in the oncoming traffic lane more often, increasing your exposure to head‑on collisions and other hazards. Even if you save a little time, your risk of a crash rises significantly.

question: When changing lanes, what is the correct way to check the area you cannot see with mirrors?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Use only the left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, you must briefly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show areas directly beside and slightly behind your vehicle where another vehicle may be hidden.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:Under no circumstances — you must not block an intersection.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:Only during rush hour traffic.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it, even with a green light. Stopping in the intersection blocks cross traffic and emergency vehicles and can cause crashes and tickets.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multi-lane one-way street onto another one-way street?
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane as long as it appears safe.,c:The center lane of the road.
note: On a one-way street, a left turn must start from the lane closest to the left curb and end in the leftmost available lane on the new street, unless signs or lane markings direct otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane and vehicles are passing you on the right, what should you do when a driver behind wants to go faster?
options: a:Stay in your lane so you don't impede traffic,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe,d:Speed up to maintain the left lane
note: The left lane is generally for passing or turning. If traffic is passing you on the right or a faster driver is behind you, move safely into the right lane when possible so you do not impede the flow of traffic.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what is the safest choice?
options: a:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap or rest.,b:Increase your speed to get to your destination sooner.,c:Turn up the radio volume to stay awake.
note: If you experience drowsiness, stop safely and rest; fighting fatigue while driving is hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and create hazards.,b:Yes — it is always a good defensive technique.,c:Yes — it is always safer than driving faster.
note: You should travel at a speed that matches the safe flow of traffic and road conditions. Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can surprise other drivers, cause sudden lane changes, and increase the risk of rear-end collisions.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to watch for workers and equipment.,c:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers are dangerous.
note: Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers or equipment are very dangerous in work zones. Following too closely leaves no time to react if traffic suddenly slows or stops, and not watching for workers, cones, and machinery increases the chance of hitting a person or object. Safe drivers slow down, increase following distance, and stay alert for changing conditions in work areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another car, how can you tell you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.,b:The other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,c:You look over your shoulder and see the passed car's right side.,d:You are one car length ahead.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed clearly in your rearview mirror. This tells you you’ve created enough space so you don’t cut the other driver off or force them to brake suddenly. Never rely on the other driver’s signal or a guess about car lengths; use your mirror and make sure the lane change can be done safely.

question: If you park uphill on a two-way street with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the side of the road (away from the center).,b:Turn them away from the side of the road (toward the center).,c:Keep them straight ahead.,d:Turn them toward oncoming traffic.
note: When you park uphill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road, not toward the center. That way, if your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway or into the shoulder instead of into oncoming traffic. The goal is always to position the wheels so a rolling vehicle moves away from the traffic lane.

question: Why is driving at night generally more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Driving at night is more hazardous mainly because you cannot see as far or as clearly as in daylight. Headlights limit how much of the road and its surroundings you can see, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce visibility. Because you see less, you have less time to detect hazards and react, so you should slow down and increase following distance at night.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:To let other drivers merge ahead of the truck.,b:Because trucks need more distance to stop.,c:To allow trucks to speed up.,d:Because truck pilots require a buffer for turns.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need more distance to stop. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver room to slow or stop safely if traffic changes. Cutting in too closely in front of a truck and then slowing down can cause a rear-end collision because the truck may not be able to stop in time.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:After it has been raining heavily for hours.,b:When the road is completely dry.,c:Just after it begins to rain.
note: Roads are usually most slippery just after it starts to rain. Oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the first water, creating a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this is washed away and traction generally improves, though you must still drive carefully.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian already in or still clearing the intersection.,b:Wait a full four seconds before moving.,c:Proceed without yielding because you have a protected turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the indicated direction, meaning oncoming traffic and conflicting movements are stopped. However, you must still yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian that is already in the intersection or still clearing it before you enter.

question: A large truck turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction:
options: a:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
note: Large trucks often need extra space to turn right because their rear wheels track inside the path of the front wheels. To avoid hitting the curb or other objects, they may swing wide. You should never try to squeeze between a turning truck and the curb.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle and to avoid being in its blind spots.,b:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.,c:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream for better fuel efficiency.
note: Following a large vehicle too closely reduces your view of the road ahead and puts you in its large blind spots, where the driver may not see you. Increasing your following distance improves your visibility and gives you more time to react if the large vehicle brakes or swerves.

question: How does stopping distance and crash severity change as speed increases?
options: a:Stopping distance and severity increase as speed increases.,b:They decrease as speed increases.,c:They are unaffected by speed.,d:Stopping distance increases but severity decreases.
note: As speed increases, your vehicle needs a longer distance to stop because both reaction distance and braking distance grow. Crash severity also increases with speed because the force of impact rises sharply, making injuries and damage more serious at higher speeds.

question: What behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision or unusual incident.,c:Using public transportation.,d:Keeping a steady speed.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or something unusual on the road is called rubbernecking. It makes traffic bunch up and can cause rear‑end collisions. To keep traffic flowing smoothly, maintain a safe, steady speed and focus on driving instead of distractions on the roadside.

question: To improve visibility reduced by rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without creating extra glare.

question: On roads where traffic is moving 50–55 mph, how is your accident risk minimized?
options: a:By driving a few mph faster than most traffic.,b:By traveling within the flow of traffic.,c:By driving much slower than the flow.,d:By constantly changing speeds to match others.
