note: On higher‑speed roads, your safest speed is usually the same general speed as surrounding traffic, as long as it is within the posted speed limit and safe for conditions. Large speed differences—either much faster or much slower than other vehicles—increase the chance of conflicts and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane must you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning left from a one‑way street, you must start your turn from the lane closest to the left curb, unless signs or lane markings say otherwise. Turning from the far‑left lane keeps your path predictable and prevents you from cutting across other lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing a vehicle, what should you confirm?
options: a:That the passed vehicle honks to allow you back.,b:That you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:That you flash your headlights as a signal.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This means you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and can return without forcing the driver to slow or brake suddenly.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what is permitted?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle.

question: From which vehicle areas should you remove snow, frost, and ice before driving?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows and mirrors.,c:Only the windshield and passenger window.
note: Before driving, you should clear snow, frost, and ice from all windows and mirrors so you have an unobstructed view in every direction. Good visibility is essential for spotting other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards, and many states can ticket you for driving with obscured windows.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Follow the driver ahead closely.,b:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,c:Pass other vehicles whenever possible.
note: In work zones you should slow down, avoid tailgating, and keep a larger following distance than usual. This gives you more time to react to sudden stops, lane shifts, or workers and equipment entering the roadway, and it helps prevent rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian began crossing after the Dont Walk signal and is in the roadway when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian has crossed before going.
note: Vehicles must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection; wait until they finish crossing before proceeding even when your light turns green.

question: What is one effective way to reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently to warn others.,c:Talk on your cell phone to calm down.
note: Signaling every lane change and turn helps other drivers understand your intentions, which reduces confusion, surprises, and conflicts that can lead to road rage. Courteous, predictable driving and following traffic laws are key to preventing aggressive driving situations.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights,b:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
note: Use low-beam headlights when you are driving behind another vehicle at night. High beams can reflect in the mirrors and blind or distract the driver ahead, increasing the risk of a crash. Reserve high beams for dark roads when there is no traffic directly in front of you or coming toward you.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing in the middle of the street, what must you do?
options: a:You must stop and yield to them.,b:You do not have to stop for them.,c:Honk to make them move out of the way.
note: You must always do what is necessary to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally (jaywalking). The law does not excuse a driver from the duty to use due care. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield so you do not strike them.

question: If weather conditions are poor, what should drivers do with speed?
options: a:Decrease their speed.,b:Increase their speed.,c:Maintain normal speed.,d:Turn on cruise control.
note: In poor weather—such as rain, snow, fog, or ice—you should reduce your speed. Slower speeds give you more time to react and help account for longer stopping distances and reduced traction. Never use cruise control on slippery roads, and do not maintain or increase speed when visibility or traction is reduced.

question: If a stopped school bus in your lane has red lights flashing, what action is required?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights flash.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop only if children are visible.,d:On a divided highway, stop if you are on the same side of the divider as the bus.
note: When a school bus in your lane or on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. On a divided highway with a physical barrier or unpaved median, drivers on the opposite side are generally not required to stop, but drivers behind or approaching the bus on the same side must always stop.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow when visibility is low, a good way to make your vehicle more visible is to turn on:
options: a:Your parking lights.,b:Up the instrumental panel lights.,c:Your headlights.
note: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, turn on your low-beam headlights to make your vehicle easier to see. Headlights improve your visibility to others and help you see the road. Parking lights alone are not sufficient while driving and are not a substitute for headlights in low-visibility conditions.

question: How should you adjust speed on a narrow, winding road?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the curve quickly.,b:Decrease your speed to match conditions.,c:Maintain the normal posted speed at all times.
note: On narrow, winding roads you should slow down so you can react safely to sharp curves, limited visibility, and oncoming traffic. Posted speed limits are for ideal conditions; when the road is hazardous, you must reduce speed to match conditions.

question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must remain stopped until:
options: a:All students are off the bus.,b:The stop arm is retracted.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. The bus does not have to start moving before you may proceed; once the signals are off and the arm is in, it is no longer loading or unloading children and traffic may go if it is safe.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around them.,b:Make sure they see you before proceeding.,c:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk; stop and let them finish crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what else should you do?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Always slow down dramatically.,d:Assume nothing is there.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where another vehicle may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: How can you help drivers behind you maintain a safe following distance?
options: a:By maintaining a steady speed.,b:By driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:By braking unexpectedly.,d:By frequently changing lanes.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early gives drivers behind you time to react and adjust their following distance. Sudden braking or frequent lane changes make it harder for them to maintain a safe space cushion.

question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:The child will always follow traffic laws.,b:The child may act unpredictably; expect the unexpected.,c:The child will yield to your vehicle.,d:You should beep to make them move.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable and may not fully understand or follow traffic rules. When you see a child riding near your vehicle, you should slow down, be ready to stop, and expect sudden or unexpected movements into your path.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance (3–4 seconds).,b:Drive more slowly than the motorcycle.,c:Be ready to use your horn constantly.,d:Tailgate to prevent lane changes.
note: Motorcycles are smaller, can stop quickly, and are less stable than cars, so they need extra space. Use at least a 3–4 second following distance so you have enough time to react if the motorcycle slows or stops suddenly.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Scanning the environment and staying focused,b:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions,c:Getting adequate rest and staying alert,d:Using signals when changing lanes
note: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions are major causes of crashes because they reduce your time to react and increase stopping distance. Safe habits like scanning, signaling, and staying rested and alert help prevent collisions.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires have less grip and it takes longer to stop. You should reduce your speed and drive smoothly so you can maintain control and have more time to react.

question: If your tires seem to lift off the road surface, what should you do first?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.,b:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly to slow down.,c:Shift into a lower gear to reduce speed.
note: If your tires start to ride on water and lose contact with the road (hydroplaning), gently ease off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or make sudden moves until your tires regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right on an interstate, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when safe.,b:Slow down drastically.,c:Stay in your lane and maintain position.
note: On multi-lane highways and interstates, it is safer to move out of the right lane when you see vehicles entering from on-ramps, if traffic allows. Changing to the left lane gives merging drivers more space and time to enter smoothly and reduces sudden braking or lane changes near the ramp.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Drive faster than the train to beat it.,b:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must use extra caution. You should slow if needed, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop if a train is coming. Never try to beat a train and never drive around lowered gates or barriers, as trains cannot stop quickly.

question: Which of these statements about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:They disappear if you have outside mirrors on both sides.,b:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be fully checked with mirrors only.,d:Blind spots are only present at high speeds.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors and must check by turning your head. Large trucks have much bigger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars, especially on the right side and directly behind them. Because of this, you should avoid lingering alongside or close behind large trucks.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger vehicles and therefore need more distance and time to stop, even with good brakes. Drivers should not cut closely in front of trucks or assume they can stop quickly; always leave extra space when merging or changing lanes near a large truck.

question: To help prevent skids on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: On slippery roads, sudden braking or turning can cause a skid. It is safer to slow down before you enter curves and intersections so you can steer smoothly through them. Adjusting your speed in advance reduces the need for hard braking while turning, which helps maintain traction.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is prohibited.,c:Passing on the right is allowed.,d:Both directions may pass freely.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing on the left is allowed when it is safe. You may cross the line to pass if the lane is clear of oncoming traffic and you can complete the maneuver without speeding or cutting off other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:Only if you accelerate before the turn.,b:If traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the right.,c:If traffic on that street is moving to the left and no sign prohibits the turn.
note: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if traffic on the street you are entering flows to the left, you make the turn from the proper lane, and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Always yield to pedestrians and other traffic before turning.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, what should you still do?
options: a:Always wear both lap and shoulder seat belts.,b:Rely on airbags and forgo seat belts.,c:Wear only the lap belt.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. You should always wear both the lap and shoulder belt so you stay properly positioned and restrained in a crash, reducing the risk of serious injury even if the airbag deploys.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered distracted driving?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,c:It is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it can take your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, and your mind off driving. This combination greatly increases the chance of missing hazards, reacting too slowly, or drifting out of your lane.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing.,b:You must stop when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,c:You should always speed up to cross faster.,d:Never expect trains to be present at crossings.
note: Trains always have the right-of-way at railroad crossings. You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or active warning device tells you to, and you should never try to beat a train. Always look and listen for trains and be prepared to stop even if you do not see one immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what speed should you aim for?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway so you can merge smoothly.,b:Five to ten mph slower than the freeway traffic.,c:The posted speed limit for unrelated freeway traffic regardless of flow.
note: On a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic (as long as it is safe and not above the speed limit). Entering too slowly forces other drivers to brake or swerve, which increases the risk of a collision.

question: What should you do to check a vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction of the blind spot.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use the outside mirror only.,d:Assume mirrors show the blind spot.
note: Mirrors do not show the areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots while still keeping your main attention on the road ahead.

question: Backing your vehicle is:
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Any time you back up, your view is more limited and it is harder to react to hazards, so backing is always considered a risky maneuver. Move slowly, check all mirrors, look over your shoulder, and use a helper when available to reduce the danger.

question: Where should a driver watch while operating the vehicle?
options: a:Only directly in front of the car.,b:Only at the center of the road ahead.,c:To the sides, ahead, and behind the vehicle.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the whole traffic picture: far ahead to anticipate problems, to the sides for pedestrians and cross traffic, and behind using mirrors. This wide awareness gives you more time to react and avoid sudden emergencies.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and slow down.,b:Change lanes and keep your speed steady.,c:Speed up to clear the area.,d:Ignore the signs if no workers are visible.
note: Orange signs and cones mark a work zone. You must slow down, follow posted work‑zone speed limits, and be ready for lane shifts, stopped traffic, and workers or equipment near the roadway, even if you do not immediately see them.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow signal, how must you proceed?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Maintain your normal speed.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look for traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and proceed only when it is safe. Treat it as a warning that cross traffic may not be fully controlled.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.,d:Never; signals are unnecessary in parking.
note: You should always signal when changing your position in traffic, including when moving toward the curb to park and when pulling away from the curb to re-enter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions so they can react safely.

question: To make quick, safe turns you should place your hands:
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,b:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
note: For good control, especially when turning quickly, place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel, typically around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions. This gives you better leverage, balance, and control than holding the wheel at the top or top-and-bottom.

question: What should you do when taking any medication and planning to drive?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how it may affect driving.,b:Open your window and drive faster.,c:Have someone follow you home.,d:Drive only during daylight.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or otherwise impair your driving. Always check with your doctor or pharmacist and read the label to see if it is safe to drive, and never drive if a medication affects your alertness or coordination.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you're driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and steer quickly to the right.,b:Use the brakes lightly and slow down gradually.,c:Pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, stay off the brakes at first, and gently ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows down gradually. Once you have the car under control and your speed has dropped, brake lightly as needed and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is classified as a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity, which impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving unsafe even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

question: Who must drivers obey at construction sites giving traffic instructions?
options: a:Security guards in parking lots.,b:Flaggers (signal persons) directing traffic.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are disabled.,d:Construction workers only.
note: Drivers must obey directions from flaggers (signal persons) in construction or work zones. Flaggers help control traffic to protect workers and drivers, and their instructions have the same legal authority as traffic signs or signals in that area.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:The speed limit is increased at night.,b:There are fewer cars on the road at night.,c:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.
note: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far ahead, and headlights provide limited and uneven lighting. This makes it harder to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving, so you must slow down and increase following distance.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes, reducing visibility.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: In fog or mist, high beams shine into the water droplets and reflect back toward your eyes, creating glare and reducing how far you can see. Use low beams or fog lights so the light aims down at the road and improves visibility instead of bouncing back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When parked on a hill or slope, you should turn your wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, it will move toward the curb or edge of the road, not into traffic. On level ground, and when waiting to turn at an intersection, your wheels should remain pointed straight ahead until you actually begin the turn.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do about braking?
options: a:Brake lightly to regain control.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to control the vehicle.,c:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, sudden braking usually makes the skid worse because it can lock the wheels and reduce your ability to steer. Instead, ease off the accelerator and stay off the brakes while you gently steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. As the vehicle straightens out and you regain traction, you can then brake smoothly if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and have checked your blind spot. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver. A fixed distance or a single car length is not a reliable or safe measure because speeds and conditions vary.

question: How close to another vehicle must you be to switch from high beams to low beams?
options: a:Within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle.,b:Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.,c:When following within about 200–300 feet of another vehicle.,d:Only when the other driver flashes their headlights at you.
note: You must use low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following within 500 feet of another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You plan to make a left turn at the next corner. To whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to vehicles turning left as well.,b:All approaching vehicles and pedestrians with the right-of-way.,c:Only to pedestrians waiting at the curb.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk with the right-of-way. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming vehicles and the crosswalk is clear before you turn. This prevents collisions with vehicles going straight or pedestrians crossing in front of you.

question: If your vehicle has an anti-lock braking system and you must stop on snow or ice, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes manually.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle roll to a stop.
note: With anti-lock brakes (ABS), you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it down. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup and helps you maintain steering control during hard stops, even on snow or ice. Do not pump the brakes yourself and do not release the pedal when you feel the pulsing; that pulsing is the ABS working.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:
options: a:The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,b:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:The yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.
note: A double yellow centerline means traffic is moving in opposite directions. You may only pass when the line next to your lane is broken, and only when it is safe. If the line next to your lane is solid, you must not cross it to pass, even if the other side is broken.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, who goes first?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,c:Wait until the intersection is empty.,d:The largest vehicle goes first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, each driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion when there are no signs or signals.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

question: At a school crossing sign, you should:
options: a:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You are not required to stop every time unless a sign, signal, or crossing guard requires it or children are actually crossing.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is waiting to cross at a corner, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Wait until the person has crossed the street and is clear of your path.,b:Tell the pedestrian when it is safe to cross.,c:Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
note: A pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is blind or visually impaired and has the right‑of‑way. You must stop and wait until the person has completely crossed and is clear of your path before turning, giving them extra time and space as needed.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery and treacherous?
options: a:Just after rain begins, when oil and dirt combine with water to form a greasy film.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:One to two hours into a rainstorm.
note: Roads are most slippery at the beginning of a rainstorm because oil, grease, and other residues that have built up on the dry pavement mix with the first water to form a slick film. Slow down, increase following distance, and avoid sudden braking or sharp steering when rain first starts.

question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted when safe.,b:Both lanes are going the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited.,d:The lane ends ahead.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line between lanes means the lanes carry traffic in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it can be done safely. You may cross the broken yellow line to pass another vehicle if you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic or other hazards.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red light must be treated the same as a stop sign. You are required to come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then look for other vehicles and pedestrians and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: For drivers 21 and older it is illegal to drive with a BAC of:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In all U.S. states, including Mississippi, it is illegal for drivers 21 and older to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. Even below 0.08%, alcohol can impair driving, but 0.08% is the per se legal limit for adult drivers.

question: Which of these slows reaction time and impairs driving ability?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Working hard.,c:Sleeping well.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the central nervous system. It reduces reaction time, impairs judgment, and affects coordination and vision, all of which make safe driving much more difficult and greatly increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is blocking an intersection when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter to assert right-of-way.,b:Wait outside the intersection until you can clear it completely.,c:Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic clears.,d:Honk to clear traffic.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through it without stopping. Even if your light is green, entering when traffic is backed up can leave you stuck in the intersection when the light changes, blocking cross traffic and risking a citation.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian waves you on.,b:Only if the pedestrian is using a phone.,c:Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. You must slow or stop as needed so the pedestrian can cross safely, regardless of whether they signal you or what they are doing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane and blind spot are clear.,b:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down significantly before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This ensures there is no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle in the area you cannot see in your mirrors before you move.

question: When a school bus has its stop arm out and red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the bus retracts the arm and the lights turn off.,b:Sound your horn before passing on the left.,c:Proceed if you think most children are finished exiting.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. This protects children who may be crossing the road and can appear suddenly from in front of or behind the bus.

question: How should you behave when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch workers.,b:Slow down, obey signs, and avoid staring at the work while maintaining a safe following distance.,c:Decrease your following distance.,d:Pass quickly without regard to signs.
note: In construction zones, you should slow down, obey all signs and flaggers, and avoid staring at the work. Maintain a larger following distance so you have more time to react to sudden stops or lane shifts and to protect workers and other drivers.

question: What are 'no zones' around large trucks?
options: a:Are areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close that they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop and maneuver safely,b:Provide several car lengths of safe following distance behind a truck,c:Are places where it is safest for cars to pass a truck,d:Are areas where trucks must yield to cars
note: No-zones are the large blind spots around trucks and buses—directly in front, directly behind, and along both sides—where a car may not be visible to the truck driver or may be so close that the truck cannot safely stop or maneuver. Staying out of these areas gives the truck driver enough space to see you and react safely.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Continue ahead; the motorist has the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Slow down early, be prepared to stop, and wait until pedestrians have completely crossed your lane before proceeding. Never drive around pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes hard immediately.,b:Grasp the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and allow the car to slow gradually.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal.,d:Turn sharply to the side of the road.
note: When a tire suddenly goes flat, the key is to keep control of the vehicle. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, then signal and move off the road to a safe place once the car has slowed.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, which action is recommended?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and immediately steer to the shoulder.
note: In a blowout, the vehicle may pull to one side. Grip the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and let the car slow down gradually while keeping it straight. Once you have control and your speed is reduced, signal and carefully move out of the traffic lane to a safe location. Avoid slamming on the brakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver approach right-of-way rules in traffic?
options: a:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.,b:Assume all other drivers will obey right-of-way rules.,c:Assume most drivers obey the rules.
note: Right-of-way rules do not guarantee you can proceed; they only describe who should go first. To prevent collisions, you should always be prepared to yield, even if you legally have the right-of-way, because other drivers may make mistakes or fail to yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When another vehicle is passing you, how should you respond?
options: a:Brake hard to prevent being passed.,b:Maintain a steady speed and position.,c:Speed up to block the pass.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane, maintain a steady speed, and do not try to speed up or block them. This gives the passing driver a predictable, stable situation so they can complete the pass safely and return to the lane without sudden braking or swerving.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both alertness and coordination are affected.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your brain and body, reducing alertness and coordination. This makes it harder to notice hazards, judge distances and speeds, and control the steering, brakes, and pedals smoothly, which greatly increases crash risk.

question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:After you have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,c:When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle so you do not cut them off or force them to brake suddenly.

question: What do double solid yellow centerlines on the roadway mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing only allowed from your direction.,d:Passing allowed only during daylight.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean you may not cross the lines to pass from either direction. They are used where visibility or road conditions make passing unsafe, so you must stay in your lane except when making a permitted left turn across the lines.

question: What is a common problem caused by continuous hard braking on ice or snow?
options: a:It helps you stop faster.,b:It can lock the wheels and cause loss of steering.,c:It keeps brakes from freezing.,d:It improves traction.
note: On ice or snow, hard continuous braking can cause your wheels to lock, which makes the tires slide instead of roll. When the wheels are locked, you lose steering control and the vehicle can skid straight ahead, even if you turn the steering wheel.

question: How much following distance should you maintain for every 10 mph of speed?
options: a:One car length for every 10 mph.,b:One-half car length for every 10 mph.,c:Three car lengths for every 10 mph.,d:Two car lengths for every 10 mph.
note: A common rule of thumb is to allow about one car length of following distance for every 10 mph of speed in good conditions. This gives you more time and space to react and stop if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly. In poor weather or low visibility, you should increase your following distance beyond this basic guideline.

question: If the center of a multilane road has a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.,b:Passing is allowed only from the side next to the dashed line.,c:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,d:Both sides may pass.
note: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only the traffic on the side with the dashed line may cross the center line to pass, and only when it is safe. The traffic on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross the line to pass.

question: Before entering an intersection, what sequence should you use to look for hazards?
options: a:Look left, then right, then left again.,b:Look only to your left.,c:Look only to your right.
note: Before entering an intersection, look left first, then right, then left again. Traffic coming from your left is closer to you and will reach the intersection sooner, so you double-check that direction before you move. Also scan ahead and, when appropriate, quickly check behind for any hazards.

question: Why should you signal continuously while making a turn?
options: a:It lets other road users know your intentions.,b:It is illegal to turn off your signal early.,c:It always shortens travel time.,d:It makes the turn safer even if not needed.
note: You should signal well in advance and keep your signal on continuously through the turn so that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians clearly understand where you intend to go. This advance warning helps them adjust their speed or position and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas of the roadway that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using only your mirrors. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head to check these areas over your shoulder to be sure there are no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles hidden in your blind spots.

question: What is a likely consequence of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:It can provoke and frustrate other drivers.,b:It cannot result in a traffic citation.,c:It helps prevent being cut off and reduces collisions.
note: Tailgating (following too closely) is dangerous because it greatly reduces your time to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops. It can also anger or frighten other drivers, increasing the risk of road rage or sudden braking. In many states, following too closely is a ticketable offense.

question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane where there is no marked crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Make eye contact and then pass.,b:Slow down briefly as you pass.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,d:Signal and proceed normally.
note: Even without a crosswalk, you must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and let them finish crossing.

question: When should you increase the gap between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,b:When following a small passenger vehicle.,c:When driving more slowly than the posted speed.
note: If another driver is following you too closely, you should increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead. This larger cushion gives you more time to slow or stop gradually, reducing the chance that the tailgater will hit you from behind.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Brake as hard as possible until the skid stops.,c:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Avoid slamming on the brakes, because that can make the skid worse. If your vehicle has ABS and you must brake, apply firm, steady pressure while continuing to steer.

question: Is it legal to drive while taking medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If prescribed by a doctor.,c:If you do not feel drowsy.
note: It is illegal to drive if any medication—prescription or over-the-counter—impairs your ability to drive safely. The key issue is impairment, not whether a doctor prescribed it or how you feel. Always read warning labels and follow your doctor’s advice about driving while using a medication.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent has what effect on crash risk?
options: a:It roughly doubles your chances of being in a fatal crash.,b:It will not have any effect on your driving.,c:It will not put other drivers at risk.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol in your system can affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Research shows that crash risk begins to rise at BAC levels as low as 0.02%, especially for serious and fatal crashes. Because you are already less alert and more likely to make mistakes, your chances of being involved in a fatal crash are higher even at this low BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you intend to pass another vehicle, what is a safe assumption?
options: a:Do not assume the other driver will make space for you to return.,b:Assume the other driver will let you back in if you signal.,c:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.
note: When passing, you must never rely on other drivers to create space or behave predictably. You are responsible for making sure there is enough clear road ahead and enough room to return to your lane safely without forcing the other driver to slow or move. Do not assume the other driver will slow down, move over, or maintain a steady speed.

question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be just as dangerous as speeding because it causes other drivers to brake, change lanes, or attempt risky passes. On many roads, especially freeways, you are required to keep up with the flow of traffic (within the speed limit) or use the right lane. If you unnecessarily block or impede traffic, you may be cited.

question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount.
note: Mississippi has zero tolerance for drivers under 21; any detectable amount of alcohol can lead to license suspension.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.,b:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,c:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem while driving, you should first signal and carefully move off the roadway to the shoulder or a safe area, then turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you. Stopping in a traffic lane is extremely dangerous and should be done only if the vehicle cannot be moved at all.

question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed and create a hazard for following vehicles?
options: a:When driving up long or steep hills.,b:When driving down long, gradual hills.,c:When driving through long, gradual curves.
note: Large trucks are heavy and lose speed when climbing long or steep hills. This can surprise drivers following too closely, so you should allow extra space, be prepared for slower speeds, and only pass when it is safe and legal.

question: How should a driver check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Glance over the appropriate shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Only use the left outside mirror.,c:Rely solely on the inside rearview mirror.,d:Assume mirrors show all areas.
note: Mirrors do not show the areas directly alongside your vehicle, called blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly glance over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward to check that no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in that blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,b:The right-hand lane may pass.,c:Both lanes may pass.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only when turning left safely into or out of a driveway or side road, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Because motorcycles do not obey traffic laws.,b:Because motorcycles can stop much more quickly than a typical vehicle.,c:Because motorcycles always drive slower than cars.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can often stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcycle brakes suddenly, greatly increasing the risk of a rear-end collision. Always leave extra following distance behind motorcycles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you signal your intention to turn?
options: a:At least 100 feet before beginning the turn.,b:About 50 feet before the turn.,c:About 10 feet before the turn.
note: You should signal well before you turn so others have time to react. In most areas, you must signal at least 100 feet before turning in regular conditions, and often 200 feet or more when driving at higher speeds, such as on highways.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: As daylight fades or visibility decreases, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road. Parking lights or emergency flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Expect oncoming traffic to yield to you.,c:Complete the turn without yielding if you have a green light.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Even with a green light, you only turn when it is safe and the way is clear.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, trucks carrying hazardous materials, etc.).,b:Watch for multiple trains.,c:Both of the above.
note: At railroad crossings, you must be alert for vehicles that are required to stop at all tracks, such as school buses and many hazardous materials trucks, and you must also watch for more than one train that may be approaching on multiple tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley or driveway and crossing a sidewalk to enter the street, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed if no pedestrians are visible.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.
note: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot across a sidewalk, you must stop before the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians and any traffic on the sidewalk or street. Only proceed when the sidewalk and roadway are clear.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection instruct you to do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed through the intersection only with caution. You do not need to stop unless conditions require it for safety.

question: To prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.,d:Drive in the center of the lane only.
note: Reducing speed in rain helps your tires maintain contact with the road surface. At higher speeds, water can build up under the tires and cause hydroplaning, where you lose steering and braking control. Slowing down is the primary way to prevent this.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: At a Yield sign, you must give the right-of-way to any traffic already in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard. You must slow down and be prepared to stop; if other vehicles or pedestrians would be affected by your movement, you must let them go first.

question: Which road area is most likely to remain icy in cold, wet weather?
options: a:A hilly open road.,b:A residential street.,c:A shaded section of roadway.
note: Shaded road sections stay colder because they get less sunlight, so ice forms sooner and melts later there. In cold, wet weather, these shaded spots can remain icy even when the rest of the road looks clear, so you should approach them with extra caution.

question: What should you do to reduce glare from an oncoming vehicle's headlights?
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road, then resume looking ahead.,b:Keep your focus fixed on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams to warn the other driver.
note: When facing glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This keeps you in your lane while avoiding direct glare that can temporarily blind you. Do not stare at the lights or flash your high beams.

question: Which behavior could identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Frequent, erratic, or improper lane changes.,b:Driving slowly below the speed limit.,c:Having many passengers in the vehicle.
note: Aggressive drivers often show unsafe behaviors such as frequent, sudden, or improper lane changes, tailgating, and speeding. These actions increase crash risk. If you see this behavior, create space and avoid engaging with the driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the statutory speed limit on U.S. or State four-lane highways in Mississippi unless otherwise posted?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: In Mississippi, the statutory maximum speed limit for passenger automobiles on U.S. or State four-lane highways is 65 mph unless a different limit is posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum speed limit on interstate highways and four-lane highways in Mississippi under normal driving conditions?
options: a:30 mph,b:35 mph,c:40 mph,d:45 mph
note: In Mississippi, the statutory minimum speed limit on both interstate highways and U.S. or State four-lane highways is 40 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit for a school bus transporting children to or from school on regular routes in Mississippi?
options: a:35 mph,b:45 mph,c:55 mph,d:65 mph
note: In Mississippi, the maximum speed limit for a school bus while transporting children on regular routes is 45 mph, or 65 mph on the interstate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Mississippi, what is the maximum speed limit for a school bus on the interstate system?
options: a:45 mph,b:55 mph,c:60 mph,d:65 mph
note: In Mississippi, the maximum speed limit for a school bus while operating on the interstate system is 65 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the fee to reinstate a driver's license in Mississippi following a suspension (other than for a DUI or unpaid tickets)?
note: The reinstatement fee for most standard suspensions in Mississippi (excluding DUI or unpaid traffic tickets) is $100.
